# Change log: 09 Misc Clinical

## 2026-06-29

Initial build of the **09 Misc Clinical** knowledge base from 65 PubMed source articles (`/Users/wanjun/Downloads/benchmark_corpus/09_misc_clinical/papers`).

- **Ingest:** all 65 `.txt` sources converted into `raw/` via `bokf convert`.
- **Extraction:** sources curated in 13 thematic batches (forensic odontology/ameloglyphics; mesenchymal stem-cell therapy for radiation-induced xerostomia; premenstrual dysphoric disorder/PMS; calabash-chalk geophagy & lead toxicity; Pilates for pregnancy-related lumbopelvic pain; drug-induced hiccups; hypertrophic pachymeningitis; biomedical-informatics tools/databases; scoliosis surgical wound closure).
- **Result:** 65 `Publication` source nodes + 394 typed concept nodes, 1498 edges (≈752 substantive + 746 auto-generated `reported_in` provenance links). Every edge carries the provenance triplet (`knowledge_level`, `agent_type`, `primary_source`); numeric findings (effect sizes, ORs/HRs, p-values, doses, sample sizes) live on edges as attributes.
- **Validation:** `bokf verify` → ok (0 errors). Remaining: 5 `edge.contradiction` warnings that capture genuine cross-paper evidential tension (land vs aqua Pilates on flexibility; PMDD vs major depression; metoclopramide hiccup indication vs a single-case failure; salted vs unsalted calabash chalk on RBC count; MSC therapy dose-limiting toxicity), plus 17 benign `direction` infos on constitutive `expressed_in`/`regulates` edges. Two mistyped software "datasets" retyped to MethodOrProcedure; duplicate MESRIX trial node merged; external reference databases and trials anchored via `xref` (infores/clinicaltrials CURIEs).

anatomy/brain.body:
# Brain

The central organ of the nervous system. In the fetus/neonate the blood-brain barrier is immature, allowing heavy metals such as lead and aluminium from calabash chalk to reach the developing brain; investigated for neurodevelopmental toxicity in rat pups.

anatomy/diaphragm.body:
# Diaphragm

The principal muscle of respiration; its sudden involuntary spasmodic contraction, coordinated with the intercostal muscles and glottic closure, produces hiccups.

anatomy/dura-mater.body:
# Dura mater

The outermost, tough fibrous layer of the meninges surrounding the brain and spinal cord. It is the tissue thickened and inflamed in hypertrophic pachymeningitis.

anatomy/falx-cerebri.body:
# Falx cerebri

A sickle-shaped fold of dura mater that descends between the two cerebral hemispheres. The posterior falx, together with the tentorium cerebelli, is a preferentially involved site in idiopathic hypertrophic pachymeningitis and the substrate of the Eiffel-by-night sign.

anatomy/hamstring-muscle.body:
# Hamstring muscles

The posterior thigh muscle group originating at the ischial tuberosity of the pelvis; their extensibility governs lumbo-pelvic rhythm during forward trunk flexion, and reduced extensibility is associated with low back pain, disc problems, and injury risk.

anatomy/hip-joint.body:
# Hip joint

The articulation between the femur and the acetabulum of the pelvis, with surrounding flexor and abductor musculature; stabilization and strengthening of hip joint muscles by Pilates is linked to reduced pelvic pain and improved pelvic tilt during pregnancy.

anatomy/hippocampus.body:
# Hippocampus

A medial temporal lobe brain structure important for learning, memory and a site of adult neurogenesis; its CA1, CA3 and dentate gyrus regions were assessed for neuronal, proliferative and glial changes after prenatal calabash chalk exposure.

anatomy/lip.body:
# Lip

The soft, movable structures surrounding the oral aperture; the grooves/furrows on the red part of the lips form individual-specific lip print patterns used in cheiloscopy for forensic identification.

anatomy/lumbar-spine.body:
# Lumbar spine

The lower segment of the vertebral column comprising the lumbar vertebrae; during pregnancy it undergoes increased lordotic curvature, and Pilates core-strengthening targets the muscles around it to improve spinal stability.

anatomy/lumbo-pelvic-region.body:
# Lumbo-pelvic region

The central body region comprising the lumbar spine, pelvis, and surrounding deep stabilizing musculature (transversus abdominis, multifidus, diaphragm, pelvic floor); the target of core-stability exercise such as Pilates.

anatomy/minor-salivary-gland.body:
# Minor salivary gland

Small mucous-secreting salivary glands distributed throughout the oral mucosa; a source of adult epithelial stem/progenitor cells (hMSGSCs) used for salivary gland organoid generation.

anatomy/oesophagus.body:
# Oesophagus

The muscular tube conducting food from the pharynx to the stomach; in calabash-chalk-treated rats its squamous epithelium showed acanthosis, hyperkeratosis and koilocytosis.

anatomy/oral-cavity.body:
# Oral cavity

The mouth cavity whose health depends on saliva for lubrication; an organ at risk during radiotherapy whose increased dose during stem-cell-sparing planning can raise dysphagia risk.

anatomy/palatal-rugae.body:
# Palatal rugae

Irregular, asymmetric ridges of the mucous membrane extending from the incisive papilla on the anterior hard palate; well-protected and highly resistant to trauma, disease and decomposition, with individual-specific patterns used in rugoscopy.

anatomy/parotid-gland.body:
# parotid gland

The largest salivary gland, the major contributor to stimulated saliva. Parotid-sparing intensity-modulated radiotherapy reduces but does not eliminate xerostomia, and sparing of stem-cell-rich regions within the parotid is a proposed prevention strategy.

anatomy/parotid-stem-cell-rich-region.body:
# Parotid stem-cell-rich region

A subvolume of the parotid gland particularly rich in stem cells; preclinical and clinical data show that radiation dose to this region is critical for preserving gland function and is a stronger xerostomia risk factor than mean dose to the whole parotid gland.

anatomy/pelvic-floor.body:
# Pelvic floor

The group of muscles forming the base of the pelvis; one of the deep local muscles (with transversus abdominis, diaphragm, and multifidus) activated by Pilates breath-and-core control to contribute to lumbopelvic stability.

anatomy/phrenic-nerve.body:
# Phrenic nerve

The nerve innervating the diaphragm; it forms both afferent and efferent limbs of the hiccup reflex arc, and increased phrenic excitability or spasm leads to hiccups.

anatomy/placenta.body:
# Placenta

The feto-maternal organ mediating exchange between mother and fetus; lead, aluminium, vanadium and persistent organic pollutants from calabash chalk cross the placental barrier, beginning as early as the 12th week of gestation, exposing the fetus.

anatomy/prefrontal-cortex.body:
# Prefrontal cortex

A brain region critical for affective regulation; estrogen regulates blood flow and dopamine metabolism in the prefrontal cortex, providing a basis for estrogen receptor signaling influencing affect in PMDD.

anatomy/salivary-gland.body:
# salivary gland

Exocrine glands producing saliva, composed of serous and mucous acinar cells, myoepithelial cells, a ductal system, and supporting stroma. They are highly radiosensitive and their co-irradiation during head and neck radiotherapy causes hyposalivation and xerostomia.

anatomy/salivary-gland-duct.body:
# salivary gland duct

The ductal network (intercalated, striated, excretory ducts) of the salivary gland that modifies saliva composition. Label-retaining, ligation and marker studies localize salivary gland stem/progenitor cells primarily to this ductal compartment.

anatomy/somatosensory-cortex.body:
# Somatosensory cortex

The region of the cerebral cortex that processes somatosensory information; examined histologically and immunohistochemically for neuronal and proliferative changes after prenatal calabash chalk exposure in rat pups.

anatomy/stomach.body:
# Stomach

The muscular digestive organ that stores and churns ingested substances; in calabash-chalk-treated rats its mucosa showed oedema, haemorrhages and mononuclear inflammatory cell infiltrates.

anatomy/submandibular-gland.body:
# submandibular gland

A major salivary gland responsible for roughly two-thirds of unstimulated whole saliva. Often damaged during head and neck radiotherapy due to its proximity to regional nodes; it is the injection target of the MESRIX and MARSH stem-cell trials.

anatomy/tentorium-cerebelli.body:
# Tentorium cerebelli

A fold of dura mater that separates the cerebellum from the occipital lobes. With the posterior falx it is a characteristic site of involvement in idiopathic hypertrophic pachymeningitis and contributes to the Eiffel-by-night sign.

anatomy/tooth.body:
# Tooth

A calcified dental structure of the oral cavity composed of enamel, dentin, cementum and pulp; teeth are highly resistant to fire, desiccation and decomposition and are the most indestructible components of the human body, making them a valuable source for forensic identification.

anatomy/tooth-enamel.body:
# Tooth enamel

The hardest, most highly calcified tissue of the body forming the outer covering of the tooth crown; composed of enamel rods (prisms) and resistant to degradation, it preserves a microscopic record of growth that is unique to each tooth.

anatomy/umbilical-cord-blood.body:
# Umbilical cord blood

Fetal blood obtained from the umbilical cord at delivery, used as a representative measure of fetal exposure; umbilical cord blood lead levels reflect lead transferred across the placenta from the mother.

anatomy/uterus.body:
# Uterus

The female reproductive organ in which embryos implant and develop; in pregnant rats exposed to calabash chalk, uterine weight and the number of implantation sites and fetuses formed were reduced.

anatomy/vagus-nerve.body:
# Vagus nerve

The tenth cranial nerve; a component of the afferent limb of the hiccup reflex arc. Vagal pathways mediate gastric prokinetic effects and are implicated in drug-induced hiccups via gastrointestinal stimulation.

cell-type/adipose-derived-mesenchymal-st.body:
# adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell

Mesenchymal stem cells isolated from adipose tissue (e.g. by liposuction), an abundant and accessible source. Used as autologous therapy in the MESRIX trial; in head and neck cancer patients they enlarge serous salivary epithelium and improve salivary flow.

cell-type/ameloblast.body:
# Ameloblast

Ectoderm-derived epithelial cells that synthesize enamel by laying down enamel rods in an undulating, intertwining path; their morphology and movement during formation determine the unique enamel rod end pattern, after which they retract from the matured enamel surface.

cell-type/bone-marrow-derived-mesenchyma.body:
# bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cell

Mesenchymal stem/stromal cells isolated from bone marrow aspirate. Used as autologous therapy (e.g. interferon-gamma-stimulated, in the MARSH protocol); they ameliorate radiation-induced salivary gland damage largely through secreted growth/survival factors and paracrine niche support.
synonyms: bone marrow-derived clonal mesenchymal stem cell

cell-type/dental-pulp-stem-cell.body:
# human dental pulp stem cell

Multipotent mesenchymal-like stem cells harvested from dental pulp (e.g. discarded third molars or exfoliated deciduous teeth). They display self-renewal and multilineage differentiation, can be bioprinted into innervated salivary-gland-like organoids, and rescue irradiated salivary gland epithelial proliferation and innervation ex vivo.

cell-type/gingival-mesenchymal-stem-cell.body:
# Gingival mesenchymal stem cell

Mesenchymal stem cells isolated from the lamina propria of gingival connective tissue; abundant, easily obtainable, non-tumorigenic, with potent immunomodulatory and regenerative properties used to regenerate irradiated salivary glands.

stats.effect_size: 26.12% increase at 16 weeks (189.29 to 238.57 mL/min); 20.6% at 8 weeks

cell-type/head-and-neck-cancer-cell.body:
# head and neck cancer cell

Cultured squamous carcinoma cells representing head and neck cancer, used to test whether candidate xerostomia therapies (e.g. GDNF) accelerate tumor growth or modify radiation response.

cell-type/human-minor-salivary-gland-ste.body:
# Human minor salivary gland stem cell

Adult epithelial stem/progenitor cells isolated from human minor salivary glands expressing CD49f, CD29, KRT14/15/19 and capable of differentiating into acinar and duct cells; their stemness is maintained via Wnt pathway activation in 3D culture.

extra.name: Human minor salivary gland stem cell

synonyms: human minor salivary gland stem/progenitor cell

cell-type/mesenchymal-stem-cell.body:
# mesenchymal stem cell

Multipotent adult progenitor cells of mesodermal origin found in bone marrow, adipose, umbilical cord, and other connective tissues, capable of self-renewal and differentiation into mesodermal lineages and exerting immunomodulatory, anti-apoptotic, anti-fibrotic, angiogenic, and paracrine regenerative effects (CD73/CD90/CD105 positive, CD45 negative).

cell-type/salivary-acinar-cell.body:
# salivary acinar cell

The saliva-producing secretory cells of the salivary gland (serous and mucous). Largely postmitotic, they are lost after radiotherapy when not replenished by stem/progenitor cells, causing hyposalivation; functional acini are quantified by PAS staining.

cell-type/salivary-gland-acinar-cell.body:
# Salivary gland acinar cell

Secretory epithelial cells of the salivary gland that produce saliva components (e.g., amylase, AQP5, MUC5B); their radiation-induced damage reduces salivation and they are a regeneration target of organoid transplantation.

cell-type/salivary-gland-ductal-cell.body:
# Salivary gland ductal cell

Epithelial cells lining salivary gland ducts, marked by KRT19/KRT7/WFDC2; the predominant cell type in undifferentiated salivary gland organoids and the region harboring regenerative progenitor cells.

cell-type/salivary-gland-organoid.body:
# salivary gland organoid

A 3D in vitro mini-tissue recapitulating salivary gland architecture, generated from salivary gland or mesenchymal/dental-pulp stem cells. Functional organoids contain organized epithelial cell clusters and a neuronal network enabling secretion of salivary enzymes such as amylase and can be transplanted to rescue irradiated glands.

cell-type/salivary-gland-stem-cell.body:
# salivary gland stem/progenitor cell

Adult stem/progenitor cells residing mainly in the salivary gland ducts, capable of self-renewal and differentiation into acinar and ductal cells. Identified by markers such as c-Kit (CD117), CD24, CD29, CD49f, Sca1 and CD133; their radiation-induced sterilization causes long-term hyposalivation and their transplantation can restore gland function.

cell-type/umbilical-cord-derived-mesench.body:
# Umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stromal cell

Mesenchymal stromal stem cells derived from umbilical cord tissue, characterized by noninvasive collection, high proliferation rate, low immunogenicity, and strong immunomodulatory potential; proposed as an off-the-shelf allogeneic therapy for post-radiation xerostomia.

concept/biometric-trait-uniqueness.body:
# Biometric trait uniqueness

The property of a biometric characteristic by which each individual's expression of the trait is distinct and irreproducible, allowing one individual to be distinguished from another; a core requirement for a valid biometric identification tool.

concept/biometric-uniqueness.body:
# Biometric uniqueness

The principle that a biometric trait is highly unique to each individual, stable over time, easily obtainable and distinguishable, forming the basis for its use in personal identification; applied to tooth prints, lip prints and fingerprints.

concept/dental-print-media-publication.body:
# Dental print media case publication

The practice of publishing an unidentified cadaver's dental x-rays and treatment records in dental journals/newsletters so that recognizing dentists can contribute to identification; in a German survey only 3% of cases were resolved this way.
synonyms: police announcement in dental print media

concept/mass-disaster.body:
# Mass disaster

A chaotic destructive event producing multiple fatalities that require identification (e.g., aviation accidents, earthquakes, tsunamis, fires, bomb blasts), often involving severe mutilation, charring and decomposition that defeats routine identification and necessitates dental hard-tissue methods.

concept/personal-identification.body:
# Personal identification

The forensic process of establishing the identity of a living or deceased individual, especially when bodies are decomposed, burned, mutilated or skeletonized; achieved by comparing unique biometric or dental characteristics with antemortem records.

dataset/bioasq-synergy-dataset.body:
# BioASQ Synergy dataset

The publicly available dataset generated during the first three versions of BioASQ Synergy comprising 256 unique COVID-19 questions (yes/no, factoid, list, summary), related documents, snippets and ideal answers, together with expert feedback and material evolution information.

dataset/biocyc.body:
# BioCyc

A collection of pathway/genome databases of metabolic pathways and enzymes from which BioPAXViz pathway data are typically obtained.

dataset/bionda.body:
# BIONDA

A free, text-mining-based online relational database of published molecular biomarkers and biomarker candidates (genes, proteins, miRNAs) for all diseases, extracted automatically from Europe PMC abstracts and updated monthly, with biomarker-disease pairs scored by a chi-square-based reliability score.

dataset/cord-19.body:
# CORD-19

A continually updated corpus of COVID-19-related scientific articles; the only source of articles considered in each round of BioASQ Synergy for retrieving documents and snippets to answer COVID-19 questions.

dataset/disease-ontology.body:
# Disease Ontology

A curated ontology of human diseases used as a dictionary for named entity recognition and normalization of disease terms in BIONDA.

dataset/europe-pmc.body:
# Europe PMC

A free biomedical literature database whose publication abstracts are imported via the Europe PMC API as the raw text source for BIONDA's biomarker text-mining pipeline.

dataset/mirbase.body:
# miRBase

A reference database of microRNA sequences and annotations used as a dictionary for recognizing and normalizing miRNA terms in BIONDA.

dataset/protein-data-bank.body:
# Protein Data Bank

A repository of experimentally determined protein structures from which the 566 class-I pMHC crystal structures used to build RankMHC's training/evaluation dataset were downloaded.

dataset/uniprot.body:
# UniProt

A comprehensive protein sequence and annotation database used as a dictionary for recognizing and normalizing gene/protein terms in BIONDA.

disease/acquired-immunodeficiency-syndro.body:
# Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome

An immunodeficiency state caused by HIV infection; the patient in the moxifloxacin case had a 10-year history of AIDS and was on antiretroviral therapy.

disease/anca-associated-vasculitis.body:
# ANCA-associated vasculitis

A group of small-vessel vasculitides associated with anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA), including granulomatosis with polyangiitis, microscopic polyangiitis, and eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis. Hypertrophic pachymeningitis can affect up to 4.5% of AAV patients as an initial presentation or during relapse.

disease/appendicitis.body:
# Appendicitis

Acute inflammation of the appendix; in the cefotaxime case it presented as an intra-abdominal abscess from a ruptured appendix, treated surgically with antibiotic cover.

disease/covid-19.body:
# COVID-19

The infectious disease caused by SARS-CoV-2; the initial focus area of BioASQ Synergy open research questions and the subject of biomarker entries in BIONDA.

disease/dysthymia.body:
# Dysthymic disorder

A chronic, low-grade depressive disorder used as a comparator for the impairment and quality-of-life burden of PMDD, which during the late luteal phase was found to be very similar in severity to dysthymia.

disease/esophagitis.body:
# Esophagitis

Inflammation of the esophagus; drug- or pill-induced esophagitis results from prolonged mucosal contact with offending oral medications such as doxycycline, and can present with esophageal erosion and ulceration.

disease/gastritis.body:
# Gastritis

Inflammation of the stomach lining; lead intake from substances such as calabash chalk has been implicated in gastritis along with nausea, vomiting and constipation.

disease/generalized-anxiety-disorder.body:
# Generalized anxiety disorder

An anxiety disorder marked by excessive, persistent worry; women with severe premenstrual complaints are reported to be at greater risk for GAD, and adolescent girls with PMDD show higher prevalence of GAD.

disease/granulomatosis-with-polyangiitis.body:
# Granulomatosis with polyangiitis

A necrotizing granulomatous small-vessel vasculitis and a major form of ANCA-associated vasculitis. It is recognized as the primary CNS manifestation cause of hypertrophic pachymeningitis among AAV, and most AAV patients with HP are diagnosed with GPA.

disease/head-and-neck-cancer.body:
# head and neck cancer

Malignancy arising in the head and neck region (including oropharynx). The majority of patients are treated with radiotherapy, alone or with chemotherapy and/or surgery, which co-irradiates the salivary glands and causes xerostomia.
synonyms: head and neck squamous cell carcinoma

disease/hypertrophic-pachymeningitis.body:
# Hypertrophic pachymeningitis

A fibroinflammatory disorder characterized by localized or diffuse thickening of the cranial or spinal dura mater, leading to progressive neurological deficits through compression of brain parenchyma, cranial nerves, or spinal cord and intracranial hypertension. It may be idiopathic or secondary to immune-mediated, infectious, or malignant causes.

disease/idiopathic-hypertrophic-pachymen.body:
# Idiopathic hypertrophic pachymeningitis

A fibrosing inflammatory process of unknown cause involving the dura mater, especially the posterior falx cerebri and tentorium cerebelli, with dense fibrosis and inflammatory cell infiltration of lymphocytes and plasma cells. Diagnosed after exclusion of infections, malignancies, and systemic autoimmune diseases.

disease/igg4-related-disease.body:
# IgG4-related disease

A fibroinflammatory condition that can affect virtually any organ. IgG4-related hypertrophic pachymeningitis is an increasingly recognized manifestation and may account for a high proportion of cases once considered idiopathic.

disease/lead-poisoning.body:
# Lead poisoning

Toxicity resulting from lead exposure/accumulation; lead disrupts haemoglobin biosynthesis (anaemia), raises blood pressure, and damages the kidney, liver and brain/nervous system, with the fetus particularly vulnerable. Calabash chalk is a dietary source of lead exposure.

disease/major-depressive-disorder.body:
# Major depressive disorder

A mood disorder characterized by persistent depressed mood and loss of interest, associated with biological markers such as hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis abnormalities, and used here as a comparator for the symptomatology, comorbidity, and disease burden of PMDD.

disease/malaria.body:
# Malaria

A mosquito-borne infectious disease caused by Plasmodium parasites; Plasmodium falciparum malaria is treated with quinine plus doxycycline or tetracycline.

disease/malignancy.body:
# Malignancy

Neoplastic disease (including dural carcinomatosis, meningioma, meningeal lymphoma, and metastatic disease) that can cause secondary hypertrophic pachymeningitis. Malignancy-associated HP cases were less likely to achieve remission and had higher mortality.

disease/neuromuscular-scoliosis.body:
# Neuromuscular scoliosis

A spinal deformity caused by myopathy or upper/lower motor neuron disease (e.g., cerebral palsy, muscular dystrophy, spinal muscular atrophy). Patients have higher rates of postoperative wound complications than adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients.

disease/oral-mucositis.body:
# Oral mucositis

Inflammation and ulceration of the oral mucosa characterized by erythema and painful ulcerative lesions; radiation-induced oral mucositis affects nearly 100% of patients undergoing head and neck radiotherapy.

disease/oropharyngeal-cancer.body:
# Oropharyngeal cancer

Malignant squamous cell carcinoma arising in the oropharynx, frequently p16/HPV-positive, commonly treated with curative-intent radiotherapy with or without chemotherapy; the predominant cancer type in the salivary stem cell xerostomia trials.
synonyms: squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx

disease/panic-disorder.body:
# Panic disorder

An anxiety disorder characterized by recurrent panic attacks; PMDD shares intriguing similarities with panic disorder, including provoked panic on lactate/CO2/CCK/flumazenil challenge, response to low-dose clomipramine, and altered respiratory and benzodiazepine sensitivity.

disease/parkinson-disease.body:
# Parkinson's disease

A progressive neurodegenerative movement disorder characterized by resting tremor, rigidity and bradykinesia, treated with dopaminergic agents. Synucleinopathy affecting the brainstem may predispose to hiccups, which occur more frequently in PD patients than healthy controls.

disease/pharyngitis.body:
# Pharyngitis

Inflammation of the pharynx, often of infectious origin; in the azithromycin case it was the indication for the antibiotic that was associated with persistent hiccups.

disease/polycystic-ovary-syndrome.body:
# Polycystic ovary syndrome

An endocrine disorder of reproductive-age women that can mimic PMS/PMDD symptoms and is associated with markedly increased risk of depression and anxiety, warranting investigation when patients fail to respond to multiple SSRI agents.

stats.effect_size: 3.39x increased risk of depression; 3.64x increased risk of anxiety

disease/postpartum-depression.body:
# Postpartum depression

A reproductive affective mood disorder occurring after childbirth; treated by the proprietary intravenous allopregnanolone formulation brexanolone, which acts via positive allosteric modulation of GABA-A receptors, and in which brexanolone also decreases serum 3a,5a-androsterone.

disease/premenstrual-dysphoric-disorder.body:
# Premenstrual dysphoric disorder

A severe variant of premenstrual syndrome characterized by psychiatric symptoms (irritability, affective lability, depressed mood, anxiety/tension) that recur regularly during the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle and remit shortly after the onset of menstruation; defined in DSM-5 requiring at least five symptoms with one core affective symptom and marked functional impairment, affecting approximately 2-8% of women of reproductive age.

stats.effect_size: 46.2% prevalence of irritability vs 30.8% depressed mood; interview confirmation 97%, daily rating 92%
15.8% suicide attempts in subthreshold PMDD group
Q-LES-Q percent of total score 60.0 (luteal) vs 81.0 (follicular)
~3.835 years (1400 days) of disability per woman; ~14,492,465 total DALYs estimated for USA
correlation r=0.522; PMDD prevalence 63.2% in those with depression vs 17.5% without; chi-square 23.93
correlation r=0.534; PMDD prevalence 57.9% in those with anxiety vs 14.6% without; chi-square 24.52

disease/premenstrual-syndrome.body:
# Premenstrual syndrome

A recurrent cluster of psychological and/or physical symptoms appearing during the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle and resolving by the end of menstruation; a broad and poorly defined diagnosis that may involve somatic symptoms, mental symptoms, or both, of which PMDD is the severe psychiatric form.

disease/sarcoidosis.body:
# Sarcoidosis

A systemic granulomatous disorder of unknown cause that is one of the systemic autoimmune/vasculitic etiologies of secondary hypertrophic pachymeningitis.

disease/schizophrenia.body:
# Schizophrenia

A chronic psychotic disorder; copy number variations at the esv2730987 and nsv1177513 sites of GABRB2 and SNPs in GABRB2 have been associated with schizophrenia in addition to PMDD, indicating shared genetic susceptibility through GABA-A receptor genes.

disease/scoliosis.body:
# Scoliosis

A lateral curvature and rotational deformity of the spine. In these studies it is primarily nonidiopathic (syndromic or neuromuscular) scoliosis requiring surgical correction.

disease/secondary-hypertrophic-pachymeni.body:
# Secondary hypertrophic pachymeningitis

Hypertrophic pachymeningitis attributable to an identifiable underlying cause, including infections (tuberculosis, fungal, syphilis), systemic autoimmune/vasculitic disorders (granulomatosis with polyangiitis, sarcoidosis, rheumatoid arthritis), IgG4-related disease, and malignancies.

disease/sjogren-syndrome.body:
# Sjogren's syndrome

An autoimmune disorder in which lymphocytic infiltration and inflammatory mediators damage exocrine glands, producing hyposalivation and xerostomia; one of the most frequent non-radiation causes of dry mouth and a common preclinical model.

disease/tuberculosis.body:
# Tuberculosis

An infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. As a cause of secondary/infectious hypertrophic pachymeningitis it was a leading etiology in studied cohorts and is associated with leptomeningeal involvement, brain parenchymal lesions, arterial stroke, and hypoglycorrhachia.

disease/xerostomia.body:
# xerostomia

The subjective condition of dry mouth, frequently a complication of radiotherapy for head and neck cancer. It results from salivary gland hypofunction/hyposalivation and severely impairs quality of life; current treatments only provide temporary symptom relief.

exposure/acid-exposure.body:
# Acid exposure

Exposure of teeth/bodies to concentrated acid (e.g., 36.46% hydrochloric acid) as occurs in acid attack injuries or chemical destruction of a body; tooth prints remain reproducible after such exposure.

exposure/caffeine-intake.body:
# Caffeine intake

Consumption of caffeine, a central nervous system stimulant; higher caffeine intake is an independent risk factor for PMDD in adult working women, potentially through hyperactivation of the central nervous system that triggers or exacerbates anxiety symptoms.

exposure/calabash-chalk-consumption.body:
# Calabash chalk consumption

The act of consuming (eating/ingesting) calabash chalk, a geophagic clay, typically orally and often during pregnancy as a remedy for morning sickness; it is the behavioural exposure through which lead, aluminium and other contaminants in the chalk reach the body and fetus.

stats.effect_size: implantations present in only 75% (400 mg/kg) and 25% (800 mg/kg) of rats; absent in ~85% overall
up to 57.9% abortion; resorption observed (control had zero resorption)

exposure/early-age-at-menarche.body:
# Early age at menarche

Onset of the first menstrual period at a younger age; identified as an independent factor positively associated with PMDD in adult working women, possibly via accelerated reproductive development and altered hormonal regulation.

exposure/geophagy.body:
# Geophagy

The deliberate practice of eating earth, soil, clay or chalk; a non-food craving behaviour (form of pica) common across cultures and social classes, practised for pleasure, medicinal, religious or dietary reasons. Consumption of calabash chalk is a specific form of geophagy.

exposure/high-temperature-exposure.body:
# High temperature exposure

Exposure of teeth/bodies to high temperatures (e.g., fire, incineration up to 750 degrees C and beyond) as occurs in burn victims, fires and cremation; teeth and enamel rod end patterns are highly resistant to such exposure.

exposure/ionizing-radiation.body:
# Ionizing radiation

Exposure to ionizing radiation delivered during radiotherapy or used experimentally (e.g., 7.5-15 Gy in mice) to ablate salivary gland stem cells and induce hyposalivation and xerostomia.

exposure/menstrual-cycle-luteal-phase.body:
# Luteal phase of the menstrual cycle

The phase of the menstrual cycle after ovulation and before menstruation, characterized by high gonadal steroid levels; the temporal window during which premenstrual dysphoric symptoms surface and after which (with menstruation onset) they remit.

extra.name: Luteal phase of the menstrual cycle

exposure/physical-activity.body:
# Physical activity

Participation in sports or exercise of consistent frequency and duration; regular physical activity is associated with lower PMDD risk and improved premenstrual symptoms, while irregular physical activity is an independent risk factor in adult working women.

food/calabash-chalk.body:
# Calabash chalk (Nzu)

A naturally occurring geophagic mineral/clay material composed chiefly of fossilised seashells or of clay and mud (kaolin clay group, aluminium silicate hydroxide Al2Si2O5(OH)4), sold as powder, pellets or moulded blocks. It is consumed in Nigeria, West Africa and beyond, especially by pregnant women as an antiemetic for morning sickness, and contains toxic heavy metals/metalloids including lead, aluminium and arsenic.

function/horizontal-gene-transfer.body:
# Horizontal gene transfer

The transfer of genetic material between organisms other than by descent; its discovery is feasible through inspection of pathway variants from distant species along the phylogeny in BioPAXViz.

function/metabolic-pathway-evolution.body:
# Metabolic pathway evolution

The divergent evolution and emergence of metabolic pathways across organisms, which BioPAXViz is designed to help study by combining enzyme presence/absence patterns, pathway variants and species phylogeny.

gene/esr1.body:
# Estrogen receptor alpha gene

The gene encoding estrogen receptor alpha, a nuclear receptor mediating estrogen signaling; intronic polymorphic variants of ESR1, particularly in intron 4, are associated with PMDD and with personality traits that distinguish PMDD patients from controls.

gene/gabrb2.body:
# GABRB2

The gene encoding the beta-2 subunit of the GABA-A receptor; SNPs in GABRB2 are associated with schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, heroin addiction, and autism, and CNV alterations at its esv2730987 and nsv1177513 sites are significantly associated with PMDD and schizophrenia in Chinese populations.
synonyms: gamma-aminobutyric acid type A receptor beta2

measure/anti-neutrophil-cytoplasmic-anti.body:
# Anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody

Autoantibodies directed against neutrophil cytoplasmic antigens (proteinase 3 / PR3 and myeloperoxidase / MPO), measured by indirect immunofluorescence or ELISA. They define ANCA-associated vasculitis; PR3-ANCA and MPO-ANCA subtypes differ in their hypertrophic pachymeningitis presentations.

measure/blood-lead-level.body:
# Blood lead level

The concentration of lead measured in blood (e.g., ug/dl), a biomarker of lead exposure and body burden; levels even below 10 ug/dl are toxic, especially to the fetus, with CDC historically recommending <10 ug/dl in children.

measure/body-composition.body:
# Body composition

Anthropometric measures of body constitution including percentage of body fat, body mass index, body fat mass, and skeletal muscle mass, assessed by bioelectrical impedance analysis; used to evaluate body-fat metabolism changes during pregnancy.

measure/cerebrospinal-fluid-protein.body:
# Cerebrospinal fluid protein

Protein concentration in the cerebrospinal fluid, measured during evaluation of hypertrophic pachymeningitis. CSF parameters could not differentiate idiopathic from secondary HP in the studied cohort.

measure/daily-record-of-severity-of-prob.body:
# Daily Record of Severity of Problems

A prospective daily symptom chart rating the eleven DSM criterion symptoms of PMDD plus three impairment items on a 1-6 scale, used to confirm PMDD diagnosis and to measure treatment response; total scores range from 14 to 84 per cycle phase.

extra.name: Daily Record of Severity of Problems

measure/disability.body:
# Disability

The degree of functional impairment due to low back/lumbopelvic pain, assessed by validated questionnaires such as the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI, 0-100%) and the Roland-Morris Disability Questionnaire (RMDQ, 0-24), with higher scores indicating greater disability.

measure/disability-adjusted-life-year.body:
# Disability-adjusted life year

A composite measure expressing years of healthy life lost to premature death and disability; used in the Global Burden of Disease model to quantify the substantial cumulative burden of PMS/PMDD over the reproductive lifespan.

measure/dsm-5-pmdd-criteria.body:
# DSM-5 PMDD diagnostic criteria

The American Psychiatric Association DSM-5 diagnostic criteria for PMDD requiring at least five of eleven symptoms in the premenstrual week with remission after menses onset, including at least one core affective symptom (irritability/anger, affective lability, depressed mood/hopelessness, or anxiety/tension).

measure/dsm-iv-pmdd-criteria.body:
# DSM-IV PMDD research diagnostic criteria

The four research diagnostic criteria for PMDD in DSM-IV requiring at least five of eleven symptoms (one affective) confined to the late luteal phase, marked functional interference, distinction from exacerbation of another disorder, and confirmation by prospective daily ratings over two cycles.

measure/erythrocyte-sedimentation-rate.body:
# Erythrocyte sedimentation rate

The rate at which red blood cells sediment in one hour (mm/hr); increases with anaemia and inflammation, and was significantly raised by non-salted calabash chalk in female Wistar rats.

measure/flexibility.body:
# Flexibility

The range of motion of a joint or joints, including low back, hip, and hamstring extensibility, commonly assessed by linear tests (sit-and-reach, toe-touch) or angular tests; reduced extensibility is associated with low back pain risk.
synonyms: low back and hip joint flexibility

measure/gad-7.body:
# Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 questionnaire

A seven-item self-report screening scale for generalized anxiety disorder; used to assess anxiety severity in adolescent girls, where scores correlated positively with PMDD severity.

measure/haemoglobin-concentration.body:
# Haemoglobin concentration

The concentration of haemoglobin in blood (g/dl), reflecting oxygen-carrying capacity; reduced after non-salted calabash chalk exposure in female Wistar rats.

measure/hypertrophic-pachymeningitis-cli.body:
# Hypertrophic pachymeningitis composite clinical score

A composite clinical disability score (maximum 23) summing graded severity of headache, encephalopathy/seizure, visual symptoms, ataxia, hemiparesis, and cranial nerve dysfunction, adapted from validated stroke/headache/ataxia scales to quantify and follow neurological disability in hypertrophic pachymeningitis patients.

measure/length-of-hospital-stay.body:
# Length of hospital stay

The number of days a patient remains hospitalized following the index spinal fusion surgery.

measure/lumbopelvic-stability.body:
# Lumbo-pelvic stability

The ability to maintain segmental stability and mobility control of the core body (lumbo-pelvic region) via proper activation of deep trunk muscles, assessed using a pressure biofeedback unit (pass/fail); poor control is an early sign of back problems.

measure/maternal-body-weight.body:
# Maternal body weight gain

The increase in maternal body weight during gestation, an index of maternal health and pregnancy progression; inhibited dose-dependently in pregnant Wistar rats exposed to calabash chalk.

measure/mini-international-neuropsychiat.body:
# Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview-Plus

A short structured diagnostic interview for DSM-IV and ICD-10 psychiatric disorders, used to ascertain the presence of PMDD; demonstrated high inter-rater reliability with a Kappa coefficient of 0.82 in the working-women prevalence study.

measure/molecular-biomarker.body:
# Molecular biomarker

A measurable indicator (variation or expression pattern of a gene, protein or miRNA) of a specific biological process, condition or state including disease; biomarker-disease co-occurrence pairs are the core entities organized by BIONDA.

measure/muscle-strength.body:
# Muscle strength

The maximal force generated by a muscle or muscle group, here measured isometrically (e.g., hip flexion and hip abduction) using a manual muscle strength meter via the active straight-leg-raise method.

measure/naranjo-adverse-drug-reaction-pr.body:
# Naranjo adverse drug reaction probability scale

A standardized scoring instrument for estimating the probability that an adverse event is caused by a drug, classifying causality as doubtful, possible, probable or definite based on temporal sequence, prior reports, dechallenge/rechallenge and alternative explanations.

extra.name: Naranjo adverse drug reaction probability scale

measure/normal-tissue-complication-proba.body:
# Normal tissue complication probability

A modeled probability that a normal organ at risk will develop a radiation-induced complication, derived from validated dose-response models and used to estimate and compare side-effect risks (e.g., xerostomia, dysphagia) between radiotherapy plans.

measure/operative-time.body:
# Operative time

The total duration of the spinal fusion surgical procedure, including the wound closure step.

measure/pain-intensity.body:
# Pain intensity

A patient-reported measure of perceived pain severity, typically assessed on a 0-10 cm Visual Analog Scale (VAS) ranging from 0 (no pain) to 10 (most pain); used to quantify lumbopelvic/low back pain severity.

measure/phq-9.body:
# Patient Health Questionnaire-9

A nine-item self-report depression screening questionnaire; used to assess depression severity in adolescent girls, where scores correlated positively with PMDD severity.

measure/pup-birth-weight.body:
# Pup birth weight

Body weight of offspring at birth; significantly lower in pups of dams given 800 mg/kg calabash chalk, with recovery after exposure ceased.

measure/quality-of-life.body:
# Quality of life

A multidimensional patient-reported outcome capturing the impact of disease and treatment. In these studies it is assessed with xerostomia-specific questionnaires (XQ, XeQOL) and visual analog scales; radiation-induced xerostomia dramatically reduces quality of life.
synonyms: Quality of Life Enjoyment and Satisfaction Questionnaire

measure/radiation-dose.body:
# Radiation dose

Dosimetric quantification of ionizing radiation delivered to tissue, reported as mean dose (Dmean) in Gray and dose-volume metrics (e.g., V15Gy, V30Gy); mean dose to parotid stem-cell-rich regions is a key risk factor for xerostomia.

measure/red-blood-cell-count.body:
# Red blood cell count

The number of red blood cells per unit volume of blood; a reduced count indicates anaemia and was significantly lowered by non-salted calabash chalk in female Wistar rats.

measure/reoperation-rate.body:
# Reoperation rate

The proportion of patients requiring an unplanned return to the operating room for additional surgery within the postoperative follow-up window after spinal fusion.
synonyms: rate of unplanned return to OR

measure/salivary-amylase-activity.body:
# Salivary amylase activity

Activity or content of alpha-amylase in saliva or gland tissue, a marker of acinar secretory function used to assess salivary gland recovery after MSC therapy in irradiated models.

measure/salivary-flow-rate.body:
# salivary flow rate

The volume of saliva produced per unit time (mL/min in humans), the principal objective measure of salivary gland function. Measured under unstimulated (resting) or stimulated conditions and used to quantify radiation-induced hyposalivation and treatment response.

measure/salivary-gland-volume.body:
# Salivary gland volume

The contoured volume of a salivary gland (e.g., parotid or submandibular) measured on planning CT; baseline parotid gland volume predicts malnutrition in irradiated head-and-neck cancer patients.

stats.effect_size: baseline cumulative parotid volume < 55.3 cm3 associated with malnutrition

measure/salivary-lag-time.body:
# Salivary lag time

The latency between stimulation and onset of salivary secretion, used as a functional outcome of salivary gland recovery in irradiated rodent models; shortened by MSC therapy.

measure/sleep-quality.body:
# Sleep quality

A measure of sleep quality and sleep disturbances over the past month, most commonly assessed with the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), a self-report scale (0-21) where higher scores indicate worse sleep; a score >=5 indicates poor sleep quality.

measure/social-adjustment-scale.body:
# Social Adjustment Scale (self-report)

A self-report instrument measuring social and role functioning across work, housework, social/leisure, marital, parental, and family domains; lower scores reflect better functioning, and PMDD women show marked luteal-phase impairment comparable to other depressions.

measure/stimulated-whole-saliva-flow-rat.body:
# Stimulated whole saliva flow rate

Saliva flow rate measured during gustatory or mechanical stimulation (e.g., chewing wax), expressed in mL/min; a secondary endpoint in stem cell xerostomia trials.

measure/surface-righting-reflex.body:
# Surface righting reflex

A developmental neurobehavioural test of vestibular and motor function measuring a pup's ability to return to a standing position from supine; transiently delayed in 800 mg/kg calabash chalk pups at PND 7.

measure/umbilical-cord-blood-lead-level.body:
# Umbilical cord blood lead level

The concentration of lead measured in umbilical cord blood at delivery, a biomarker of fetal lead exposure; measured by atomic absorption spectrometry to assess transplacental lead transfer associated with maternal calabash chalk consumption.

measure/unstimulated-whole-saliva-flow-r.body:
# unstimulated whole saliva flow rate

The resting whole-mouth saliva flow rate (mL/min), measured by the drooling/spitting method. Salivary gland hypofunction is defined as <=0.20 mL/min and hyposalivation as <=0.10 mL/min; it was the primary efficacy outcome of the MESRIX trial.

method/acetate-peel-technique.body:
# Acetate peel technique

A method of recording enamel rod end patterns in which acetone dissolves a cellulose acetate film (or cellophane tape) placed on the tooth surface, replicating the surface irregularities; originally developed by palaeobotanists, it is a simple, low-cost, reliable way to obtain tooth prints.

method/acid-etching.body:
# Acid etching of enamel

Application of acid (commonly 10% or 37% orthophosphoric/phosphoric acid) to dissolve inorganic material and the smear layer from the enamel surface, exposing prism cores or peripheries to reveal enamel rod end patterns prior to recording tooth prints.

method/ameloglyphics.body:
# Ameloglyphics

The science of recording and analyzing tooth prints - the patterns formed by enamel rod ends on the tooth surface; used as a hard-tissue biometric tool for personal identification in forensic odontology (amelo = enamel, glyphics = carvings).
synonyms: study of enamel rod end patterns

method/ape-gen2.body:
# APE-Gen2.0

A rapid pMHC structural modeling tool that generates ensembles of peptide binding poses (up to 100 conformations) using Vina/Vinardo scoring and optional openMM energy minimization; used to construct the pMHC structural model database on which RankMHC was trained.

method/appendectomy.body:
# Appendectomy

Surgical removal of the appendix; performed for appendicitis/appendiceal abscess. In the cefotaxime case, hiccups developed 48 hours after appendectomy.

method/atomic-absorption-spectrometry.body:
# Atomic absorption spectrometry

An analytical technique measuring the concentration of an element by its absorption of light; used to quantify lead in umbilical cord blood of pregnant women in the Cameroon study.

method/automated-biometric-identificatio.body:
# Automated biometric identification

Automated method of identifying or verifying a living person based on physiological or behavioral characteristics using pattern recognition; in ameloglyphics, software such as VeriFinger SDK detects minutiae points to compare and match enamel rod end patterns against a database.

method/bioasq.body:
# BioASQ challenge

An international challenge on large-scale biomedical semantic indexing and question answering, running since 2012, whose benchmarks (4721 questions accumulated) and infrastructure underpin the BioASQ Synergy task.

method/bioasq-synergy.body:
# BioASQ Synergy

An iterative research process and BioASQ task implementing a continuous dialogue in which biomedical experts pose open questions, automated QA systems retrieve documents/snippets and generate answers, and expert feedback is fed back to improve subsequent rounds; initially focused on COVID-19.

method/bioelectrical-impedance-analysis.body:
# Bioelectrical impedance analysis

A non-invasive method of assessing body composition, used to derive fat-free mass index and diagnose malnutrition in irradiated head-and-neck cancer patients.

method/biometric-software-analysis.body:
# Automated biometric tooth-print analysis

Automated comparison of tooth prints (or fingerprints) using fingerprint-recognition software (e.g., Verifinger SDK, AFIS) that detects minutiae points (discontinuities, line endings, dots, empty spaces) and outputs similarity scores for verification or identification.

method/biopax-format.body:
# BioPAX

A community standard file format for sharing biological pathway data; BioPAXViz accepts template and modified BioPAX files (with presence/absence flags for proteins/pathways) as input.

method/biopaxclient.body:
# BioPAXClient

A Java console application that adds presence/absence flags to Pathway and ProteinReference elements of a BioPAX file via custom comments, producing the modified BioPAX files used as input to BioPAXViz.

method/biopaxviz.body:
# BioPAXViz

A Cytoscape (version 3) application implemented in Java using the OSGi model that parses, views and browses metabolic pathways from BioPAX files and performs visual comparative analysis of metabolic pathway topologies across pathway phylogenomic profiles given a species phylogeny. Distributed under the MIT License at the CGU-CERTH GitHub repository.

method/bite-mark-analysis.body:
# Bite mark analysis

Forensic comparison of bite mark injuries with a suspect's dentition based on the individuality of the human occlusion profile; used in identification although considered less reliable than DNA because the dentition's hypervariation is not constant throughout life.

method/bone-marrow-derived-cell-mobiliza.body:
# bone marrow-derived cell mobilization

Mobilization of mesenchymal stem cells from bone marrow (e.g. via G-CSF) so they migrate to the salivary gland and secrete growth and survival factors that enhance regeneration by stimulating remaining salivary gland stem cells and decreasing inflammation.

method/cellophane-tape-technique.body:
# Cellophane tape technique

A method of recording enamel rod end patterns (and lip prints) by lifting the etched enamel surface pattern onto cellophane tape, which is then transferred to a glass slide or bond sheet for microscopic/biometric analysis.

method/cheiloscopy.body:
# Cheiloscopy

The forensic study and classification of the grooves/furrows on the red part of the lips (lip prints); lip groove patterns are unique to each individual and remain unchanged over time, serving as a biometric identification tool.

method/chelation-therapy.body:
# Chelation therapy

A treatment using chelating agents (e.g., calcium disodium EDTA, succimer) to bind and remove heavy metals such as lead from the body; recommended/considered for high blood lead levels in pregnancy (CDC recommends if blood lead >45 ug/dl).

stats.dose: CDC recommends if blood lead >45 ug/dl

method/co2-inhalation-challenge.body:
# Carbon dioxide inhalation challenge

A panicogenic provocation test in which CO2 inhalation elicits panic attacks; women with premenstrual dysphoria, like panic disorder patients, are sensitive to this and other anxiety-producing challenges (lactate, cholecystokinin, flumazenil).

method/cytoscape.body:
# Cytoscape

A software environment for integrated models of biomolecular interaction networks that hosts apps via its app manager; BioPAXViz is built as a Cytoscape 3.x app.

method/dactyloscopy.body:
# Dactyloscopy

The analysis of fingerprint ridge patterns of the soft tissue (dermatoglyphics) for personal identification; a conventional biometric whose reliability is limited when soft tissues are decomposed or destroyed, motivating hard-tissue alternatives such as ameloglyphics.

method/dental-age-estimation.body:
# Dental age estimation

Estimation of an individual's age from dental development and degenerative changes (tooth eruption/exfoliation, mineralization, root resorption, secondary dentine deposition, attrition, root dentine transparency, aspartic acid racemization, Gustafson method); used in forensic identification because dental maturity is largely unaffected by nutritional and endocrine status.

method/dental-dna-analysis.body:
# Dental DNA analysis

Extraction and analysis of genomic or mitochondrial DNA from dental tissues (dentin, enamel, pulp, cementum), amplified by PCR, for forensic identification; teeth protect DNA from extreme environmental conditions and provide a reliable DNA source in degraded remains.

method/dental-identification.body:
# Dental identification

A method of personal identification comparing ante-mortem and post-mortem dental records, restorations, and radiographs of an individual; one of the most reliable and frequently applied identification methods, especially for decomposed, burned or disfigured bodies.

method/dental-radiography.body:
# Dental radiography

Radiographic imaging of teeth and jaws capturing distinctive features (tooth shape, restorations, root canal fillings, root morphology, sinuses, jawbone patterns); antemortem radiographs are compared with postmortem images in a dental identification system for human identification.

method/endoscopy.body:
# Endoscopy

A procedure using an endoscope to directly visualize the upper gastrointestinal tract; used to diagnose esophageal erosion and ulceration.

method/forensic-odontology.body:
# Forensic odontology

The branch of dentistry dealing with the handling, examination and presentation of dental and paraoral evidence in legal proceedings, used for human identification of decomposed, mutilated, burned or skeletonized remains in crimes and mass disasters.

method/gnrh-analogue-ovulation-inhibitio.body:
# GnRH-analogue ovulation inhibition

Treatment with a gonadotropin-releasing hormone analogue that inhibits ovulation and suppresses cyclical ovarian steroid secretion; effectively relieves premenstrual dysphoria.

method/icp-ms.body:
# Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry

An analytical technique using an inductively coupled plasma ion source and mass spectrometry to quantify trace elements; used to measure the heavy-metal and metalloid composition of calabash chalk.

method/intensity-modulated-radiotherapy.body:
# Intensity-modulated radiotherapy

A conformal radiotherapy technique that shapes dose distributions to better spare organs at risk such as the parotid glands, reducing but not eliminating radiation-induced xerostomia.

method/intraglandular-injection.body:
# Intraglandular injection

Direct injection of a cell product or therapeutic into a salivary gland, typically ultrasound-guided; the preferred MSC delivery route for radiation-induced xerostomia, shown in meta-analysis to outperform systemic transplantation for restoring salivary flow.

stats.dose: 25x10^6 cells per submandibular gland, 0.5 mL ultrasound-guided
50x10^6 cells per parotid gland and 25x10^6 cells per submandibular gland

method/intraglandular-stem-cell-injectio.body:
# Intraglandular stem cell injection

Direct injection of mesenchymal stem cells into the major salivary glands as a regenerative treatment for radiation-induced xerostomia, as performed in the MESRIX trials (50 million ASC per parotid, 25 million per submandibular gland).

stats.effect_size: XQ summary score decreased 21.0 units (95% CI -37.5 to -4.5); sticky saliva decreased 20.0 units

stats.dose: 50 million ASC per parotid gland, 25 million per submandibular gland
stats.effect_size: stimulated salivary flow rose from 0.66 to 0.86 mL/min, +0.20 mL/min (95% CI 0.08 to 0.30), ~28%

method/intravenous-injection.body:
# Intravenous injection

Systemic delivery of a cell product into a vein; a route for MSC transplantation in which cells home to damaged salivary glands but yields a smaller effect on salivary flow than intraglandular injection in preclinical models.

stats.dose: 1x10^6 GMSCs/mL, 500 uL via lateral saphenous vein weekly for 3 weeks

method/learning-to-rank.body:
# Learning-to-Rank

A family of machine-learning ranking methodologies; RankMHC uses the LambdaMART algorithm (combining RankNet/LambdaRank with gradient-boosted regression trees, MART) with a pairwise loss as its ranking backbone.

method/magnetic-resonance-imaging.body:
# Magnetic resonance imaging

A non-invasive imaging modality, used with gadolinium contrast, that characterizes the degree of dural inflammation, localization, extent and pattern of dural thickening and enhancement, and is the key investigation for diagnosing and monitoring hypertrophic pachymeningitis.

method/meningeal-biopsy.body:
# Meningeal biopsy

Surgical sampling of the meninges and/or brain parenchyma for histopathology and culture; considered the gold standard for definitive diagnosis of hypertrophic pachymeningitis, revealing dense fibrous infiltration with lymphocytes and plasma cells in the idiopathic form.

method/mesenchymal-stem-cell-therapy.body:
# mesenchymal stem cell therapy

Therapeutic injection of mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (adipose-, bone marrow-, or dental-pulp-derived) into salivary glands, typically under ultrasound guidance, to treat radiation-induced salivary gland hypofunction and xerostomia, acting mainly through paracrine secretome effects.

method/named-entity-recognition.body:
# Named entity recognition

A dictionary-based text-mining method for automatically identifying and normalizing mentions of proteins/genes, miRNAs and diseases in biomedical abstracts, used by BIONDA with Disease Ontology, UniProt and miRBase as dictionaries.

method/network-meta-analysis.body:
# Network meta-analysis

A statistical evidence-synthesis method that indirectly compares interventions across studies via a common comparator; planned here to compare adipose- versus bone-marrow-derived MSC treatment effects on salivary flow rate.

method/oral-gavage.body:
# Oral gavage administration

A procedure for administering a measured dose of a substance directly into the stomach via an oral tube; used to administer calabash chalk suspensions to rats in the toxicity studies.

method/organoid-transplantation.body:
# Salivary gland organoid transplantation

Transplantation of salivary gland organoids (human or mouse) into damaged salivary glands to regenerate tissue and restore salivation; demonstrated as a therapeutic option for radiation-induced xerostomia in mouse models.

stats.effect_size: significant increase in saliva secretion in 1x10^5 cell mSGO transplant group from 4 to 8 weeks post-transplant

method/orthopedic-wound-closure.body:
# Orthopedic wound closure

A standard (often nonstandardized) wound closure technique performed by the orthopedic surgical team, consisting of approximation of fascia, subcutaneous tissue, and skin without specialized muscle flap reconstruction, used after posterior spinal fusion.

method/ovariectomy.body:
# Ovariectomy

Surgical or medical removal/suppression of ovarian function; effectively relieves premenstrual dysphoria by abolishing the cyclical secretion of ovarian sex steroids.

method/pandora.body:
# PANDORA

A homology-modeling-based pMHC structural modeling tool that uses MODELLER's molPDF objective scoring function; used to test the generalization of RankMHC to models from a different modeling protocol.

method/perioperative-optimization-protoc.body:
# Perioperative optimization protocol

A multidisciplinary perioperative care pathway for neuromuscular scoliosis patients undergoing spinal fusion, including indications/multidisciplinary conferences, chlorhexidine washes, antibiotic prophylaxis (cefazolin, gentamicin, intrawound vancomycin/bacitracin), and standardized intraoperative infection-prevention steps designed to reduce surgical site infections.

method/pilates.body:
# Pilates

A mind-body core-stability exercise method developed by Joseph Pilates that coordinates core-stabilizing exercise with breath control and flowing whole-body movement, activating deep trunk muscles (transversus abdominis, diaphragm, multifidus, pelvic floor) to improve lumbopelvic stability, flexibility, posture, and neuromuscular control.

method/plastic-multilayered-closure.body:
# Plastic multilayered closure

A layered surgical wound closure technique performed by a plastic surgeon, involving paraspinal muscle flap mobilization for vascularized coverage of spinal hardware, a fluid-impermeable barrier fascial layer, dead-space obliteration, and tension-free skin closure, used to reduce postoperative wound complications after spinal fusion.

method/posterior-spinal-fusion.body:
# Posterior spinal fusion

A surgical procedure to correct spinal deformity by fusing vertebrae through a posterior approach, the most common technique for surgical management of neuromuscular scoliosis. Associated with high postoperative complication rates in nonidiopathic patients.

method/prospective-daily-symptom-rating.body:
# Prospective daily symptom rating

Prospective recording of symptoms each day over two consecutive menstrual cycles, required for valid diagnosis of premenstrual disorders; yields much lower PMDD prevalence than retrospective self-report, which substantially over-diagnoses the condition.
synonyms: Daily Record of Severity of Problems

method/proton-therapy.body:
# Proton therapy

A particle radiotherapy modality that reduces dose to the parotid glands and xerostomia risk relative to photons; stem-cell-sparing planning further lowers stem-cell-region dose but with limited additional clinical benefit.

method/radiotherapy.body:
# radiotherapy

Use of ionizing radiation to treat head and neck cancer. Co-irradiation of the salivary glands causes acinar cell loss and stem-cell sterilization, leading to hyposalivation and xerostomia; parotid-sparing IMRT, stem-cell-region sparing and adaptive RT aim to reduce this toxicity.

stats.dose: single dose 10-25 Gy in preclinical models

method/randomized-controlled-trial.body:
# Randomized controlled trial

An experimental study design in which subjects are randomly allocated to intervention or control/placebo groups to assess treatment efficacy; the design used in the MESRIX-III trial and most included rodent studies.

method/rankmhc.body:
# RankMHC

A machine-learning, Learning-to-Rank-based class-I peptide-MHC binding mode identification predictor that ranks an ensemble of pMHC conformations by their LRMSD closeness to the native structure, using LambdaMART (XGBoost) on Rosetta-derived energy features and SASA/RSA, with a structure-aware average pooling that maps peptides of any length to nonamers.

method/rapid-sizer-image-editing-softwar.body:
# Rapid Sizer image editing software

A pattern-sketching/outline image editing software (Patrick Roberts, Collingwood, Ontario) used to outline enamel prism images and create sketched patterns of enamel prints for grouping and identification in ameloglyphics.

method/relation-extraction.body:
# Relation extraction

A text-mining method that identifies biomarker-disease pairs based on co-occurrence of a biomolecule and a disease in the same abstract sentence; used by BIONDA to populate biomarker-disease entries.

method/rosetta.body:
# Rosetta ref2015 scoring function

The default, latest scoring function of the Rosetta modeling suite, used in RankMHC to extract per-amino-acid and global energy-based features and also used as a baseline scoring function for ranking pMHC structural models.

method/rugoscopy.body:
# Rugoscopy

The forensic study and classification of palatal rugae (ridges of the palatal mucous membrane) for human identification; rugae are individualistic and highly resistant to trauma, disease and decomposition.

method/salisphere-culture.body:
# salisphere culture

A non-adherent in vitro suspension culture in which dissociated salivary gland cells self-aggregate into proliferating spheres (salispheres) enriched for stem/progenitor cells. Used to expand and select salivary gland stem cells (e.g. c-Kit enrichment) prior to transplantation and to assay their function.

method/salivary-gland-scintigraphy.body:
# Salivary gland scintigraphy

Nuclear medicine imaging using radiopharmaceuticals (e.g., [99mTc]pertechnetate for gland function or [99mTc]HMPAO-labeled cells for grafting/migration) to assess salivary gland parenchymal uptake, excretory fraction, and MSC retention and migration after transplantation.

method/scanning-electron-microscopy.body:
# Light/research microscopy of enamel surface replicas

An imaging technique that scans a surface with a focused electron beam to produce high-resolution topographical images; used to visualize the arrangement of enamel prisms on the tooth surface and corroborate enamel/tooth print patterns.

extra.name: Light/research microscopy of enamel surface replicas

method/secretome-therapy.body:
# cell-free secretome therapy

Cell-free regenerative strategies using stem-cell secretome components (cell soups/extracts, conditioned media, extracellular vesicles/exosomes) instead of whole cells. These restore salivary flow and protect epithelial, vascular and neural compartments in irradiated salivary glands in rodent models, and lack the immune-rejection and storage limitations of whole-cell therapy.

stats.effect_size: bone marrow soup restored flow to 0.4 mL/min; spleen 64.7%, AdSC 56.7%, labial 60% increase

method/spinal-instrumentation.body:
# Spinal instrumentation

The implantation of hardware (rods, pedicle/sacral-alar-iliac screws, etc.) to stabilize and correct the spine during fusion surgery for scoliosis.

method/stem-cell-sparing-radiotherapy.body:
# Stem cell sparing radiotherapy

A radiotherapy planning technique that adds objectives to minimize dose to the parotid stem-cell-rich regions, reducing predicted xerostomia risk without compromising target coverage; implementable with small adjustments to existing photon and proton plans.

stats.effect_size: physician-rated grade >=2 xerostomia NTCP reduced >=2% in 47% of patients; daytime xerostomia in 20%; general xerostomia >=2% reduction in 57%
median Dmean,SCR reduction 4.1 Gy ipsilateral and 3.5 Gy contralateral with photons; 2.2 and 1.9 Gy with protons
dysphagia NTCP increased >=2% in 3 of 30 (10%) patients
Dmean oral cavity increased >=2 Gy in 6 of 30 patients

method/stem-cell-transplantation.body:
# salivary gland stem cell transplantation

Transplantation (e.g. by intraglandular injection) of stem/progenitor cells into damaged salivary glands to regenerate functional gland tissue and restore saliva secretion after radiotherapy. Requires pre-RT biopsy/isolation, in vitro expansion and post-RT delivery.

method/tele-rehabilitation.body:
# Tele-rehabilitation

Remote, non-face-to-face delivery of a supervised exercise or rehabilitation program via web/IT platforms (e.g., television or tablet), enabling real-time instructor feedback and posture correction at the participant's home; here used to deliver Pilates to pregnant women during the COVID-19 pandemic.

method/three-dimensional-bioprinting.body:
# three-dimensional bioprinting of salivary gland organoids

Additive-manufacturing and magnetic 3D cell-assembly techniques that generate salivary-gland-like organoids (e.g. from dental pulp stem cells) with ductal, myoepithelial, secretory epithelial and neuronal compartments. Used for drug discovery and to stimulate epithelial growth and innervation in irradiated and healthy salivary glands.

extra.name: three-dimensional bioprinting of salivary gland organoids

method/three-dimensional-cell-culture.body:
# Three-dimensional cell culture

In vitro culture of cells in a three-dimensional matrix such as Matrigel that supports self-organization into spheres/organoids; used to maintain and enrich salivary gland stem cell properties and generate salivary gland organoids.

method/tongue-print-analysis.body:
# Tongue print analysis

Recording and analysis of the shape, color and surface texture of the tongue (lingual impression / tongue prints), which vary between individuals and even identical twins; an emerging biometric authentication tool in personal identification.

method/verifinger-sdk.body:
# VeriFinger SDK

Biometric fingerprint identification software developed by Neurotechnology (Neurotechnologia, Lithuania) in 1998; repurposed in ameloglyphics to detect minutiae points and analyze, store and match enamel rod end patterns for personal identification.

molecular-class/antibiotic.body:
# Antibiotic

Antimicrobial drugs used to treat bacterial infections. Antibiotics are a rare but recognized cause of drug-induced hiccups, accounting for about 12% of drug-associated hiccups in pharmacovigilance data.

molecular-class/benzodiazepine.body:
# Benzodiazepine

A class of GABAergic sedative-anxiolytic drugs (e.g. midazolam) that has been frequently associated with drug-induced hiccups.

molecular-class/cephalosporin.body:
# Cephalosporin

A class of beta-lactam antibiotics, including third-generation agents such as cefotaxime, cefotetan and ceftriaxone. Their beta-lactam ring shares molecular architecture with GABA, enabling GABA antagonism implicated in cephalosporin-induced hiccups.

molecular-class/combined-oral-contracept.body:
# Combined oral contraceptive

A class of estrogen-progestin contraceptive preparations that suppress the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis and ovulation; a first-line PMDD pharmacotherapy, with drospirenone-containing 24/4 regimens FDA-approved for PMDD.

molecular-class/corticosteroid.body:
# Corticosteroid

A class of steroid drugs (e.g. dexamethasone, methylprednisolone) that are among the most frequently reported pharmacological causes of drug-induced hiccups.

molecular-class/dopamine-agonist.body:
# Dopamine agonist

A class of drugs (including pramipexole and ropinirole) that stimulate dopamine receptors, used to treat Parkinson's disease. Prolonged dopamine D3 receptor and serotonergic stimulation has been linked to drug-induced hiccups.

molecular-class/fluoroquinolone.body:
# Fluoroquinolone

A class of broad-spectrum antibiotics including moxifloxacin and levofloxacin that act on bacterial DNA gyrase; several members have been associated with hiccups.

molecular-class/gabaergic-neuroactive-st.body:
# GABAergic neuroactive steroid

A class of endogenous steroid metabolites that modulate the effect of GABA at GABA-A receptors, including positive allosteric modulators (allopregnanolone, pregnanolone) and negative allosteric modulators (isoallopregnanolone, epipregnanolone); implicated in the pathophysiology and treatment response of PMDD.

molecular-class/gonadal-steroid.body:
# Gonadal sex steroid

The class of ovarian steroid hormones (including estrogen and progesterone) whose cyclical secretion across the menstrual cycle drives premenstrual symptomatology; administration of these steroids can provoke symptom relapse in PMDD women rendered symptom-free by ovulation inhibition.

molecular-class/gonadotropin-releasing-h.body:
# Gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist

A class of agents (e.g. leuprolide acetate) that suppress the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis to produce a reversible medical oophorectomy; effective in PMDD but limited by menopausal side effects from estrogen deficiency, used in severe cases unresponsive to SSRIs or COCs.

molecular-class/growth-factor.body:
# Growth factor

A family of secreted signaling proteins (e.g., VEGF, IGF-1, GM-CSF, SDF-1, FGF10) produced or enhanced by transplanted stem cells that mediate paracrine regeneration, angiogenesis, and proliferation in damaged salivary glands.

molecular-class/macrolide-antibiotic.body:
# Macrolide antibiotic

A class of antibiotics (including erythromycin, clarithromycin, roxithromycin and the related azalide azithromycin) that has been rarely associated with hiccups, possibly via a vagal mechanism.

molecular-class/major-histocompatibility.body:
# Class-I Major Histocompatibility Complex

A class of cell-surface receptors that bind peptides in their binding cleft and present them to T-cell receptors; the HLA-A*02:01 allele and nonamer peptides are the most common subjects of class-I pMHC modeling.

molecular-class/metabolic-enzyme.body:
# Metabolic enzyme

Enzymes encoded by metabolic enzyme-encoding genes that act as components (nodes) of metabolic pathways; their presence/absence across genomes constitutes the phylogenetic profiles visualized by BioPAXViz.

molecular-class/selective-serotonin-reup.body:
# Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor

A class of antidepressant drugs that increase synaptic serotonin by blocking its reuptake; the first-line pharmacotherapy for moderate-to-severe PMS/PMDD, effective in roughly 50-60% of PMDD patients with rapid onset, and reported to act additionally as brain steroidogenic stimulants that raise GABAergic neuroactive steroid levels.

molecular-class/serotonin-reuptake-inhib.body:
# Serotonin reuptake inhibitor

A class of drugs that increase synaptic serotonin by blocking its reuptake; the first-line treatment for PMDD, distinguished by superiority over non-serotonergic antidepressants, lower effective doses, and an almost immediate onset of action in PMDD compared with the 2-3 week lag in depression.

molecular-class/t-cell-receptor.body:
# T-cell receptor

Cell-surface receptors on T cells that recognize peptide-MHC complexes; downstream recognition of presented peptide antigens by T-cell receptors triggers the immune response central to the pMHC binding identification problem.

molecular-class/tetracycline-antibiotic.body:
# Tetracycline-class antibiotic

A class of broad-spectrum antibiotics including tetracycline and doxycycline, frequently associated with pill-induced esophageal injury.

molecule/3-alpha-hydroxysteroid-dehydrog.body:
# 3alpha-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase

An enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of 5alpha-dihydroprogesterone to allopregnanolone and 5beta-dihydroprogesterone to pregnanolone; sertraline decreases its Km and increases its catalytic efficiency ~10-fold for allopregnanolone production, proposed as a mechanism of SSRI action in PMDD.

molecule/5-bromo-2-deoxyuridine.body:
# 5-bromo-2'-deoxyuridine (BrdU)

A synthetic thymidine analogue incorporated into newly synthesised DNA, used as a marker for cell proliferation, migration and time of cell origin in the central nervous system; administered to label dividing cells in the rat brain neurodevelopment study.

molecule/allopregnanolone.body:
# Allopregnanolone

A progesterone-derived GABAergic neuroactive steroid that acts as a potent positive allosteric modulator of the GABA-A receptor with anxiolytic and antidepressant-like properties; its synthetic intravenous formulation (brexanolone) is FDA-approved for postpartum depression, and its dysregulation is implicated in PMDD pathophysiology.

molecule/alpha-amylase.body:
# Alpha-amylase

A salivary digestive enzyme produced by acinar cells; its activity and gene expression are used as functional readouts of salivary gland and organoid differentiation.

molecule/aluminium.body:
# Aluminium

A metal that is a major constituent of calabash chalk (aluminium silicate hydroxide / kaolin clay; ICP-MS highest concentration, 38726 mg/kg). It can cross the placental barrier and is associated with gastrointestinal effects (constipation, impaction, colicky pain, anorexia, nausea, irritation) and neurotoxicity.

molecule/amelogenin.body:
# Amelogenin

A human enamel matrix protein whose encoding gene has distinct copies on the X and Y chromosomes; the sex-specific difference in amelogenin gene patterns is exploited for sex determination of an individual in forensic odontology.

molecule/aquaporin-5.body:
# Aquaporin 5

A water-channel protein expressed in salivary gland acinar cells that enables water entry essential for saliva production; a marker of acinar differentiation and progenitor cell differentiation in salivary gland organoids.

molecule/arsenic.body:
# Arsenic

A toxic metalloid contaminant present in calabash chalk (ICP-MS 9.4 mg/kg). It is implicated in gastric distress and stomach upset, decreased haemoglobin and RBC counts, cancers (bladder, lung, skin), and poses a risk to fetal development.

molecule/azathioprine.body:
# Azathioprine

An immunosuppressive antimetabolite used as a steroid-sparing agent in hypertrophic pachymeningitis, allowing tapering of corticosteroids.

molecule/azithromycin.body:
# Azithromycin

A semisynthetic azalide (macrolide-related) antibiotic derived from erythromycin, with broad activity against respiratory pathogens. It is widely distributed in tissues with a long terminal half-life (~68 h) and has been associated with persistent hiccups via a hypothesized vagal mechanism.

molecule/baclofen.body:
# Baclofen

A GABA-B receptor agonist and analogue of gamma-aminobutyric acid used to treat persistent and intractable hiccups. It reduces neuronal excitability (cell hyperpolarization) and depresses reflex hiccup activity.

molecule/bcl-2.body:
# B-cell lymphoma 2

An anti-apoptotic protein whose upregulation indicates decreased apoptotic activity; its increased expression in MSC-treated irradiated salivary gland and mucosa reflects the anti-apoptotic protective effect of MSCs.

molecule/beta-catenin.body:
# beta-catenin

The central mediator of canonical Wnt signaling acting as an activator of gene transcription. Nuclear beta-catenin in ductal EpCAM+ cells marks active Wnt signaling driving adult salivary gland stem cells.

molecule/c-kit.body:
# c-Kit

A receptor tyrosine kinase used as the principal cell-surface marker to isolate salivary gland stem/progenitor cells. c-Kit+ salivary gland cells are located in the ducts and, when transplanted into irradiated glands, can restore saliva secretion and gland morphology.

molecule/c-x-c-chemokine-receptor-type-2.body:
# C-X-C chemokine receptor type 2

A chemokine receptor whose overexpression in MSCs upregulates P-Akt and P-Erk1/2, enhancing MSC migration and targeting to inflamed oral mucosa and improving their therapeutic effect in radiation-induced oral mucositis.

molecule/carbachol.body:
# Carbachol

A cholinergic agonist used to stimulate intracellular calcium mobilization in salivary gland organoids, demonstrating their functional secretory responsiveness.

molecule/cefotaxime.body:
# Cefotaxime

A third-generation cephalosporin antibiotic with a beta-lactam ring. It can cross the blood-brain barrier and exert antagonism of GABA neurotransmission, a proposed mechanism for cefotaxime-induced hiccups.

molecule/chir99021.body:
# CHIR99021

A small-molecule inhibitor of glycogen synthase kinase 3 beta (GSK3beta) that activates the canonical Wnt/beta-catenin pathway by allowing beta-catenin nuclear translocation, used to enrich salivary gland stem cells and inhibit their differentiation in 3D culture.

molecule/chlorpromazine.body:
# Chlorpromazine
