A phenothiazine antipsychotic and dopamine antagonist used as a treatment for hiccups.

molecule/chromium.body:
# Chromium

A heavy metal contaminant reported among the constituents of calabash chalk (ICP-MS 43 mg/kg).

molecule/cisplatin.body:
# Cisplatin

A platinum-based radiosensitizing chemotherapeutic administered concomitantly with radiotherapy (concomitant systemic therapy) in head-and-neck cancer treatment.

molecule/clomipramine.body:
# Clomipramine

A tricyclic serotonin reuptake inhibitor effective for PMDD at much lower doses (around 25 mg/day) than required for depression (150 mg/day or more), reducing premenstrual irritability and dysphoria.

stats.dose: ~25 mg/day (vs 150 mg/day or more for depression)

molecule/clusterin.body:
# clusterin

A side-population-cell-derived protein identified as a factor that helps recovery of salivary gland hypofunction, believed to scavenge reactive oxygen species after irradiation.

molecule/cyclophosphamide.body:
# Cyclophosphamide

An alkylating immunosuppressive agent used as an immunomodulatory treatment in hypertrophic pachymeningitis, particularly in immune-mediated/vasculitic forms.

molecule/dimethyl-sulfoxide.body:
# Dimethyl sulfoxide

A cryoprotectant component (10%) of the CryoStor10 freeze medium used as placebo in the MESRIX-III trial; it has potential anti-inflammatory activity and may have influenced the salivary flow increase observed in the placebo arm.

molecule/donor-specific-antibody.body:
# Donor-specific antibody

Anti-human-leukocyte-antigen alloantibodies directed against donor antigens, an indicator of immune response to allogeneic cell therapy; transient DSAs after allogeneic ASC treatment resolved by 3 years.

molecule/dopamine.body:
# Dopamine

A catecholamine neurotransmitter implicated in central processing of the hiccup reflex; dopamine antagonists are used to treat intractable hiccups while dopamine agonists have been associated with hiccups.

molecule/doublecortin.body:
# Doublecortin (DCX)

A microtubule-associated protein expressed in newly generated (immature) neurons and their dendrites, used as an immunohistochemical marker of adult neurogenesis.

molecule/doxycycline.body:
# Doxycycline

A semisynthetic tetracycline-derivative antibiotic used for treatment and prophylaxis of malaria and other infections. When dissolved it forms an acidic solution (pH ~3.0) that can cause local esophageal mucosal injury and ulceration if it lodges in the esophagus.

molecule/drospirenone.body:
# Drospirenone

A synthetic progestin used in combined oral contraceptives; the 24/4 regimen of 3 mg drospirenone with 20 mcg ethinyl estradiol is FDA-approved for management of PMDD and is more effective than placebo at reducing PMDD symptoms.

stats.dose: 3 mg drospirenone / 20 mcg ethinyl estradiol, 24/4 regimen

molecule/epidermal-growth-factor.body:
# Epidermal growth factor

A paracrine growth factor secreted by MSCs that exerts trophic effects on salivary gland acini, ducts, and mucosal epithelial cells, promoting proliferation, neovascularization, and salivary secretion while inhibiting apoptosis.

molecule/erythromycin.body:
# Erythromycin

A macrolide antibiotic with prokinetic gastrointestinal activity; it enhances gastric tone and emptying via vagally mediated pathways, relevant to the proposed vagal mechanism of macrolide-associated hiccups.

molecule/estrogen.body:
# Estrogen

An ovarian steroid sex hormone whose cyclical fluctuation across the menstrual cycle is implicated in premenstrual symptomatology; changes in estradiol levels can precipitate affective destabilization in women with PMDD, and estrogen regulates prefrontal blood flow and dopamine metabolism.

molecule/extracellular-vesicle.body:
# extracellular vesicle

Lipid-bilayer-enclosed nanovesicles (exosomes and microvesicles) secreted by cells, carrying proteins, lipids, RNA and DNA cargo. Released by mesenchymal and dental pulp stem cells, they act as stable paracrine mediators of regeneration and are explored as a cell-free therapy for salivary gland repair.

molecule/fibroblast-growth-factor-10.body:
# Fibroblast growth factor 10

An epithelial growth factor that promotes salivary gland morphogenesis and is used in organoid culture media; hypoxia-activated adipose MSCs prevented irradiation-induced salivary hypofunction through enhanced paracrine FGF10.

molecule/fluoxetine.body:
# Fluoxetine

A selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor approved (as Sarafem) for PMDD; effective in treating premenstrual dysphoria and shown to reduce sex steroid-related aggression in female rats as an animal model of premenstrual irritability.

molecule/gabapentin.body:
# Gabapentin

A GABA analogue and antiepileptic drug used for empirical treatment of persistent and intractable hiccups.

molecule/gamma-aminobutyric-acid.body:
# Gamma-aminobutyric acid

The principal inhibitory neurotransmitter in the brain that reduces cellular excitability via chloride channels; cortical GABA levels change across the menstrual cycle, declining in healthy women but increasing in women with PMDD between the follicular and mid-to-late luteal stages, implicating the GABAergic system in PMDD.

molecule/gdnf-family-receptor-alpha-1.body:
# GDNF family receptor alpha 1

The preferred co-receptor for GDNF, expressed in salivary gland stem cells and colocalizing with basal keratin marker CK14. GDNF binding to GFRalpha1 mediates activation of the RET receptor tyrosine kinase or the NCAM/FAK pathway.

molecule/glial-cell-line-derived-neurotr.body:
# glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor

A neurotrophic growth factor of the GDNF family ligands (GFL). Highly expressed in salivary gland stem cells and upregulated by radiation, it binds GFRalpha1 and signals (via RET or NCAM/FAK) to promote stem cell survival; its administration improves saliva production in irradiated glands without accelerating head and neck cancer growth.

molecule/glial-fibrillary-acidic-protein.body:
# Glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP)

An astrocyte-specific intermediate filament protein whose expression marks the presence and reactive activation of astrocytes; used as an immunohistochemical and Western-blot marker of astrocytic response in the developing rat brain.

molecule/glucocorticoid.body:
# Glucocorticoid

Anti-inflammatory steroid hormones; prednisolone (a glucocorticoid) was the preferred and most commonly used drug for treating hypertrophic pachymeningitis, typically dosed at 1-2 mg/kg for a minimum of 12 weeks.

molecule/granulocyte-colony-stimulating-.body:
# granulocyte colony-stimulating factor

A cytokine used to mobilize bone marrow cells to the salivary gland, where their secreted growth factors ameliorate radiation-induced damage and hyposalivation through stimulation of surviving endogenous salivary gland stem cells.

molecule/hepatocyte-growth-factor.body:
# Hepatocyte growth factor

A paracrine growth factor secreted by MSCs with immunosuppressive and regenerative actions, inducing proliferation of epithelial cells through the PI3K/Akt pathway and contributing to salivary gland repair.

molecule/interferon-gamma.body:
# interferon gamma

A cytokine used in the MARSH protocol to stimulate bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cells prior to cryopreservation, which preserves their immunomodulatory functionality and prevents cryopreservation-induced immune dysfunction.

molecule/isoallopregnanolone.body:
# Isoallopregnanolone

An isomer of allopregnanolone that acts as a negative allosteric modulator antagonizing allopregnanolone modulation of the GABA-A receptor; its formulation sepranolone significantly reduced PMDD symptoms in placebo-controlled trials.

molecule/keratinocyte-growth-factor.body:
# keratinocyte growth factor

A fibroblast growth factor (FGF7) that prevents radiation damage to salivary glands by expanding the stem/progenitor pool. Administration rescues radiation-induced hyposalivation in animal models when sufficient surviving stem cells remain.

molecule/lead.body:
# Lead

A toxic heavy metal contaminant present in calabash chalk (approximately 40 mg/kg, ICP-MS measured 36.8 mg/kg). About 95% of absorbed lead binds red blood cells and is stored in bone; it crosses the placenta, disrupts haemoglobin biosynthesis, and is neurotoxic, with no blood level considered safe.

molecule/leucine-rich-repeat-containing-.body:
# Leucine-rich repeat-containing G-protein coupled receptor 5

An adult stem cell marker and R-spondin receptor that potentiates Wnt signaling; its increased expression in salivary gland stem cells indicates maintained stemness during Wnt pathway activation.

molecule/levodopa.body:
# Levodopa

A dopamine precursor used as a mainstay treatment for Parkinson's disease. In the reported case it did not cause hiccups, although levodopa-induced hiccups have been described elsewhere.

molecule/methotrexate.body:
# Methotrexate

An antifolate immunosuppressant used as a steroid-sparing immunomodulatory agent in the treatment of hypertrophic pachymeningitis.

molecule/metoclopramide.body:
# Metoclopramide

A dopamine D2 receptor antagonist and 5-HT4 agonist with prokinetic and antiemetic properties, used to treat hiccups. It may relax the diaphragm via dopamine receptor effects, reduce esophageal contractions, and promote gastric emptying.

molecule/moxifloxacin.body:
# Moxifloxacin

A broad-spectrum fluoroquinolone antibiotic with activity against gram-positive, gram-negative and atypical pathogens. It is highly lipophilic and crosses the blood-brain barrier, where it can compete for or antagonize GABA receptors, a proposed mechanism for moxifloxacin-induced hiccups.

stats.latency: approximately 2 hours after first IV injection

molecule/muc5b.body:
# MUC5B

A gel-forming mucin essential for lubrication of the oral mucosa; its levels are diminished in xerostomia, and its expression in transplanted salivary gland organoids indicates improved salivary composition.

molecule/mycophenolate-mofetil.body:
# Mycophenolate mofetil

An immunosuppressive agent inhibiting inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase, used as an additional immunomodulatory drug in hypertrophic pachymeningitis.

molecule/neuronal-nuclei-antigen.body:
# Neuronal nuclei antigen (NeuN)

A neuron-specific nuclear antigen expressed in post-mitotic neurons, used as an immunohistochemical marker of neuronal differentiation and neuronal population/integrity in brain tissue.

molecule/neurturin.body:
# neurturin

A GDNF-family ligand that promotes salivary gland epithelial innervation and branching morphogenesis; recombinant neurturin or its gene protects parasympathetic function and supports regeneration of irradiated/embryonic salivary gland tissue.

molecule/noggin.body:
# Noggin

A secreted BMP antagonist that binds BMPs and prevents their interaction with cell surface receptors, reducing BMP pathway activity; added to salivary gland stem cell culture to maintain stemness (increased LGR5, MYC) and inhibit differentiation.

molecule/omeprazole.body:
# Omeprazole

A proton pump inhibitor that suppresses gastric acid secretion, used to treat doxycycline-induced esophagitis and gastroesophageal symptoms.

molecule/peptide-antigen.body:
# Peptide antigen

Short amino acid sequences (typically 8-13 residues, most commonly nonamers) that bind in the class-I MHC cleft and, when presented, can elicit a T-cell-mediated immune response; their binding pose in the MHC cleft is what RankMHC ranks.

molecule/pilocarpine.body:
# Pilocarpine

A parasympathomimetic muscarinic agonist that stimulates salivation by binding the M3 muscarinic receptor in salivary glands; used to evoke saliva secretion for measurement in animal models.

molecule/pramipexole.body:
# Pramipexole

A non-ergot dopamine agonist with high affinity for dopamine D3 receptors, used to treat Parkinson's disease. It also has mild agonistic activity on serotonergic 5-HT1A/5-HT1D pathways and has been associated with persistent hiccups.

molecule/pregnanolone.body:
# Pregnanolone

A progesterone-derived GABAergic neuroactive steroid and isomer of allopregnanolone that is a positive allosteric modulator of the GABA-A receptor with equipotent sedative effects; serum pregnanolone and the pregnanolone:progesterone ratio increased with luteal-phase sertraline treatment in PMDD.

molecule/progesterone.body:
# Progesterone

An ovarian steroid sex hormone secreted during the luteal phase and the precursor of the GABAergic neuroactive steroids allopregnanolone and pregnanolone; cyclical progesterone secretion is implicated in premenstrual symptoms although serum levels are similar between women with and without PMS.

molecule/progesterone-metabolite-androst.body:
# 3alpha,5alpha-androsterone

A neuroactive steroid derived from androsterone with weak actions at the GABA-A receptor; serum 3alpha,5alpha-androsterone significantly decreased with luteal-phase sertraline treatment in PMDD, paralleling its decrease with brexanolone in postpartum depression.

molecule/quinine.body:
# Quinine

An antimalarial alkaloid used to treat Plasmodium falciparum malaria, often combined with doxycycline or tetracycline.

molecule/ropinirole.body:
# Ropinirole

A non-ergot dopamine agonist used to treat Parkinson's disease, with mild serotonergic activity. It has been associated with dose-dependent persistent hiccups.

molecule/serotonin.body:
# Serotonin

A monoamine neurotransmitter central to the pathophysiology and treatment of PMS/PMDD; patients have lower whole-blood and platelet serotonin in the luteal phase, and serotonin-augmenting drugs alleviate symptoms while tryptophan depletion aggravates them.

molecule/sertraline.body:
# Sertraline

A selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor and first-line PMDD treatment; in addition to increasing serotonergic transmission it acts as a selective brain steroidogenic stimulant, increasing the efficiency of 3alpha-HSD to favor neuroactive steroid production, and in PMDD luteal-phase treatment increased serum pregnanolone while decreasing 3alpha,5alpha-androsterone.

molecule/sucralfate.body:
# Sucralfate

A mucosal protective agent that forms a barrier over ulcerated tissue, used in combination with omeprazole to treat doxycycline-induced esophageal ulceration; its addition led to complete resolution of hiccups.

molecule/tetracycline.body:
# Tetracycline

A broad-spectrum tetracycline-class antibiotic; the parent compound of doxycycline. Like other oral antibiotics it has been associated with local esophagitis and esophageal ulceration.

stats.dose: 250 mg orally four times a day

molecule/ulipristal-acetate.body:
# Ulipristal acetate

A selective progesterone receptor modulator acting as a progesterone antagonist; it significantly reduced PMDD symptoms compared with placebo, potentially by preventing ovulation and subsequent gonadal steroid fluctuations.

molecule/vanadium.body:
# Vanadium

A heavy metal detected in calabash chalk by ICP-MS (50 mg/kg) at levels beyond expected exposure; reported to cross the placental barrier and considered potentially deleterious, including effects on blood parameters.

molecule/vascular-endothelial-growth-fac.body:
# Vascular endothelial growth factor

A paracrine angiogenic growth factor secreted by MSCs that promotes neovascularization and increased vascular area in irradiated salivary glands, supporting tissue regeneration.

molecule/wnt3a.body:
# Wnt3A

A canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling ligand used to activate the Wnt pathway in salivary gland stem cell culture, maintaining progenitor status while inhibiting acinar differentiation.

organism/guinea-pig.body:
# Guinea pig

A rodent model sharing hormonal, immunologic, and salivary gland histological similarities with humans, used to test gingival MSC therapy for irradiated parotid gland regeneration.

organism/human.body:
# Human

Homo sapiens. Head and neck cancer patients with radiation-induced xerostomia are the target population of the salivary gland stem-cell and mesenchymal stem-cell therapies reviewed and trialed here.

organism/mouse.body:
# Mouse

Mus musculus. The principal preclinical model for irradiation-induced salivary gland injury, salivary gland stem cell isolation/transplantation, and testing of GDNF, mesenchymal stem cells and secretome therapies.

organism/mycobacterium-tuberculosis.body:
# Mycobacterium tuberculosis

The acid-fast bacterium that causes tuberculosis and is a leading infectious cause of secondary hypertrophic pachymeningitis in high-burden regions.

organism/plasmodium-falciparum.body:
# Plasmodium falciparum

The protozoan parasite responsible for the most severe form of human malaria, increasingly drug-resistant and treated with regimens including doxycycline.

organism/pseudomonas-aeruginosa.body:
# Pseudomonas aeruginosa

A Gram-negative bacterium and the most common pathogen cultured from surgical site infections in these spinal fusion wound complication cases.

organism/rat.body:
# Rat

Rattus norvegicus. Used in salivary gland radiobiology studies, including monolayer culture of salivary gland stem cells, the bath-and-shower parotid irradiation experiments, and localization of stem-cell-rich gland regions.

organism/sars-cov-2.body:
# SARS-CoV-2

The coronavirus that causes COVID-19; the subject of many BioASQ Synergy questions and the source organism of the SARS-CoV-2 epitope KLWAQCVQL used as a RankMHC case example.

organism/staphylococcus-aureus.body:
# Staphylococcus aureus

A Gram-positive bacterium cultured from surgical site infections following posterior spinal fusion in these studies.

organism/wistar-rat.body:
# Wistar rat

An outbred albino laboratory strain of the brown rat (Rattus norvegicus) widely used as a mammalian model in toxicology and reproductive/developmental studies; used here to study the systemic, gastro-oesophageal, haematological, gestational and neurodevelopmental toxicity of calabash chalk.

pathway/bmp-signaling-pathway.body:
# BMP signaling pathway

Signaling pathway of the TGF-beta superfamily transmitted through type I and II BMP receptors, important in epithelial progenitor fate selection during development; its inhibition by Noggin helps maintain salivary gland stem cell stemness and suppress differentiation.

pathway/gaba-signaling-pathway.body:
# GABA signaling pathway

The inhibitory neurotransmission pathway in which GABA binds GABA-A receptors to reduce neuronal excitability; in PMDD, altered sensitivity of GABA-A receptors to neuroactive steroids and cyclic changes in cortical GABA levels are central to disease pathophysiology, and positive allosteric modulators such as allopregnanolone potentiate this pathway.

pathway/metabolic-pathway.body:
# Metabolic pathway

A series of enzyme-catalyzed reactions; metabolic pathways and their variants across genomes are the biological entity that BioPAXViz visualizes and studies for evolutionary diversification, where pathway nodes correspond to enzymes catalyzing reactions.

pathway/pi3k-akt-signaling-pathway.body:
# PI3K-AKT signaling pathway

Pro-survival signaling cascade activated by paracrine growth factors (EGF, FGF10, HGF, VEGF) from MSCs that phosphorylates AKT and MDM2 to inhibit the p53-mediated radiation-induced apoptotic pathway and protect salivary gland epithelial cells.

pathway/progesterone-to-allopregnanolone.body:
# Progesterone to allopregnanolone conversion pathway

The enzymatic pathway converting progesterone to GABAergic neuroactive steroids: 5alpha-reductase converts progesterone to 5alpha-dihydroprogesterone then 3alpha-HSD converts it to allopregnanolone, while in parallel 5beta-reductase and 3alpha-HSD convert progesterone to pregnanolone; SSRIs act as steroidogenic stimulants modulating these enzymes.

pathway/steroid-hormone-biosynthesis-pat.body:
# Steroid hormone biosynthesis pathway

A KEGG metabolic pathway (including CYP and UGT genes) producing steroid hormones; decreased CNV gain features overlapping this pathway were identified as a major causal factor of PMDD, with the UGT1A gene cluster on chromosome 2 implicated through diagnostic CNV features.

pathway/wnt-beta-catenin-signaling-pathw.body:
# Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway

A signaling pathway essential for maintenance and activation of salivary gland stem cells. Forced/transient activation during radiotherapy prevents acute and chronic hyposalivation by inhibiting apoptosis and preserving functional salivary stem/progenitor cells, though overexpression is linked to carcinogenesis.

pathway/wnt-signaling-pathway.body:
# Wnt signaling pathway

A highly conserved signaling pathway regulating cell proliferation, migration, and differentiation. When a Wnt ligand binds Frizzled and LRP5/6, beta-catenin is stabilized, translocates to the nucleus, and activates target genes; its activation maintains salivary gland stem cell properties (increased LGR5).

phenotype/affect-lability.body:
# Affective lability

Rapid and exaggerated shifts in mood, including sudden sadness and increased sensitivity to rejection; one of the core affective DSM-5 PMDD criterion symptoms, of which at least one must be present for diagnosis.

phenotype/anaemia.body:
# Anaemia

A reduction in haemoglobin concentration and/or red blood cell count; calabash chalk (non-salted) lowered Hb and RBC and raised ESR consistent with anaemia, and pale fetuses suggestive of anaemia were observed in gestational exposure.

phenotype/anterior-pelvic-tilt.body:
# Anterior pelvic tilt

An abnormal forward (anterior) rotation of the pelvis that increases during late pregnancy due to fetal growth and shortened hip flexors, collapsing pelvic inclination, accentuating lumbar curvature, and contributing to back pain and body imbalance.

phenotype/anxiety.body:
# Anxiety

A mood state of apprehension and distress, assessed by the anxiety subscale of the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS-A, 0-21); elevated in pregnancy and associated with greater functional disability from lumbopelvic pain.

phenotype/apoptosis-of-salivary-gland-ce.body:
# Apoptosis of salivary gland cells

Programmed cell death of salivary gland acinar, ductal, endothelial, and progenitor cells, induced by ionizing radiation and contributing to gland degeneration and hyposalivation; reduced by MSC therapy.

phenotype/cranial-neuropathy.body:
# Cranial neuropathy

Dysfunction of one or more cranial nerves causing palsies; a frequent manifestation of hypertrophic pachymeningitis, with optic (second), oculomotor, and lower cranial nerves commonly affected due to compression by thickened dura.

phenotype/depressed-mood.body:
# Depressed mood

A subjective state of sadness or low mood that occurs premenstrually in a subset of PMDD sufferers; less prominent than irritability in most PMDD subjects but defining a depressed-mood subtype more closely associated with major depression.

phenotype/depression.body:
# Depression

A mood state of low affect and distress, assessed by the depression subscale of the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS-D, 0-21); commonly co-occurs with pregnancy-related lumbopelvic pain and sleep disturbance.

phenotype/dose-limiting-toxicity.body:
# dose-limiting toxicity

An adverse treatment effect serious enough to limit dosing; in the MARSH trial defined as a pain score >5 (0-10 scale) at one month post-injection or any serious adverse event within one month of bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cell injection.

phenotype/dural-thickening.body:
# Dural thickening

Focal or diffuse thickening of the dura mater with abnormal contrast enhancement on MRI; the defining radiological feature used to diagnose hypertrophic pachymeningitis.

phenotype/dysphagia.body:
# Dysphagia

Difficulty swallowing, a common acute and chronic side effect of head-and-neck radiotherapy, aggravated by xerostomia and contributing to reduced oral intake and malnutrition.

phenotype/eiffel-by-night-sign.body:
# Eiffel-by-night sign

A characteristic MRI enhancement finding in hypertrophic pachymeningitis: thickened dura in the posterior falx and tentorium showing a central hypointensity (fibrosis) with an enhancing periphery (active inflammation) on post-contrast fat-saturated T1-weighted imaging, resembling the illuminated Eiffel tower at night. It is associated with idiopathic and immune-mediated HP.

phenotype/enamel-rod-end-pattern.body:
# Enamel rod end pattern (tooth print)

The pattern formed on the enamel surface by the ends of adjacent enamel rods, reflecting ameloblast morphology and movement. Each tooth print is a combination of subpatterns (e.g., wavy branched/unbranched, linear branched/unbranched, whorl open/closed, loop, stem-like) unique to an individual tooth, used as a biometric analogous to a fingerprint.

phenotype/esophageal-ulcer.body:
# Esophageal ulcer

A mucosal ulceration of the esophagus; doxycycline-induced esophageal ulcers typically present with retrosternal pain, odynophagia and dysphagia, and in this case caused severe hiccups.

phenotype/fingerprint-pattern.body:
# Fingerprint pattern

The configuration of interleaved epidermal ridges and valleys of a fingertip, formed during 12-19 weeks of intrauterine life and fixed permanently; classified into loop, whorl and arch patterns and unique to each individual including identical twins.

phenotype/gastric-mucosal-oedema.body:
# Gastric mucosal oedema with haemorrhage

Oedema with haemorrhages and mononuclear inflammatory cell infiltrates (lymphocytes, plasma cells) in the gastric mucosa, an histopathological sign of mucosal injury observed in calabash-chalk-treated rats.

phenotype/harm-avoidance.body:
# Harm avoidance

A Tridimensional Personality Questionnaire trait reflecting a tendency to respond strongly to aversive stimuli with behavioral inhibition; significantly higher in women with PMDD than controls and associated with ESR1 intron 4 SNPs.

phenotype/headache.body:
# Headache

Pain in the head, the most common presenting symptom of hypertrophic pachymeningitis, attributed mainly to inflammation of the dura mater and sometimes to raised intracranial pressure.

phenotype/hiccup.body:
# Hiccup

An involuntary, spasmodic contraction of the diaphragm and inspiratory intercostal muscles followed by sudden closure of the glottis, producing the characteristic sound. Considered a physiologic myoclonus of the diaphragm and generated by a reflex arc. Acute hiccups last less than 48 hours.

phenotype/hypoglycorrhachia.body:
# Hypoglycorrhachia

Abnormally low glucose concentration in the cerebrospinal fluid; observed primarily in infectious and malignancy-associated hypertrophic pachymeningitis.

phenotype/hyposalivation.body:
# hyposalivation

An objective reduction in salivary output (reduced whole saliva flow rate, generally below normal). It results from radiation damage to salivary acinar cells and stem/progenitor cells and underlies the symptom of xerostomia; hyposalivation is generally defined as unstimulated whole saliva flow rate at or below 0.10 mL/min.

phenotype/insomnia.body:
# Insomnia

Difficulty initiating or maintaining sleep; highly prevalent in pregnant women (reported in up to 88% during the COVID-19 pandemic) and frequently secondary to pregnancy-related back pain.

phenotype/intractable-hiccup.body:
# Intractable hiccup

Hiccups persisting for more than one month; the most severe and treatment-resistant category of hiccups.

phenotype/irritability.body:
# Irritability

A state of easily provoked anger and reduced frustration tolerance; identified across multiple studies as the single most prominent and characteristic premenstrual symptom of PMDD, more common and more severe than depressed mood or anxiety.

phenotype/lip-print-pattern.body:
# Lip print pattern

The characteristic pattern of wrinkles and grooves on the labial mucosa (Klein's zone), classified (e.g., by Suzuki and Tsuchihashi) into vertical, branched, intersected, reticular and undetermined types; unique to each individual including monozygotic twins and used in cheiloscopy for identification and sex determination.

phenotype/low-back-pain.body:
# Low back pain

Pain localized to the lumbar region of the back, a common musculoskeletal problem affecting up to two-thirds of pregnant women and a major cause of disability; associated with reduced hamstring/low-back flexibility and impaired deep trunk muscle control.

phenotype/lumbopelvic-pain.body:
# Lumbopelvic pain

An encompassing term (recommended by Wu et al.) covering both low back pain and pelvic girdle pain, with pain occurring anywhere from the 12th rib to the gluteal fold or around the pubic symphysis; highly prevalent in the second and third trimesters of pregnancy.

phenotype/malnutrition.body:
# Malnutrition

A state of nutritional deficiency, defined in irradiated head-and-neck cancer patients by low fat-free mass index (FFMI <15 kg/m2 women, <17 kg/m2 men) and/or low body-mass index (<18.5 kg/m2); a major determinant of oncologic survival.

phenotype/neuroticism.body:
# Neuroticism

A NEO Personality Inventory five-factor domain reflecting emotional instability and negative affectivity; significantly higher in women with PMDD than controls and associated with ESR1 intron 4 SNPs.

phenotype/oesophageal-epithelial-change.body:
# Oesophageal acanthosis, hyperkeratosis and koilocytosis

Keratinised squamous epithelial changes comprising acanthosis, hyperkeratosis and koilocytic changes in the oesophageal mucosa, an histopathological sign of epithelial injury observed in calabash-chalk-treated rats.

phenotype/pelvic-girdle-pain.body:
# Pelvic girdle pain

Pain experienced between the posterior iliac crest and the gluteal fold, particularly around the sacroiliac joints and/or the pubic symphysis, commonly arising during pregnancy from impaired pelvic stability and ligamentous laxity.

phenotype/perceived-stress.body:
# Perceived stress

Self-reported level of psychological stress as measured by the Perceived Stress Scale; in adolescent girls higher perceived stress is positively correlated with and more prevalent in those with PMDD.

phenotype/peripheral-pattern-of-contrast.body:
# Peripheral pattern of dural contrast enhancement

An MRI pattern in which the thickened dura mater shows contrast enhancement at its periphery with a hypointense (fibrotic) center, in contrast to uniform or nodular enhancement. It is more commonly associated with idiopathic and immune-mediated hypertrophic pachymeningitis.

extra.name: Peripheral pattern of dural contrast enhancement

phenotype/persistent-hiccup.body:
# Persistent hiccup

Hiccups that last more than 48 hours or recur at frequent intervals; can disturb sleep and daily activities and cause complications such as hypotension and bradycardia. The principal phenotype reported across these drug-induced hiccup cases.

phenotype/reduced-implantation.body:
# Reduced uterine implantation

Absence or reduction in the number of uterine implantation sites and resulting fetuses; uterine implantations were absent in ~85% of calabash-chalk-exposed rats and reduced in the remainder.

phenotype/reduced-iq.body:
# Reduced intelligence quotient

A decline in intelligence quotient; fetal/childhood exposure to lead even below 10 ug/dl has been associated with substantial IQ loss (e.g., ~6 IQ points), among other neurodevelopmental and behavioural deficits.

phenotype/reoperation.body:
# Unplanned return to the operating room

An unanticipated return to the operating room for additional surgical intervention (commonly irrigation and debridement) to manage a wound complication after the index spinal fusion procedure.

extra.name: Unplanned return to the operating room

phenotype/salivary-gland-fibrosis.body:
# Salivary gland fibrosis

Progressive deposition of fibrous connective tissue in the salivary gland following radiation injury, contributing to acinar atrophy and loss of secretory function; attenuated by MSC therapy.

phenotype/sexual-dimorphism-in-teeth.body:
# Dental sexual dimorphism

Sex-related differences in dental dimensions and features (e.g. mandibular canine index, crown diameters, accessory ridges, Barr bodies, amelogenin gene) and in distribution of enamel rod end patterns, used in forensic odontology for sex determination of an individual.

phenotype/spinal-dural-involvement.body:
# Spinal hypertrophic pachymeningitis

Involvement of the spinal dura mater by hypertrophic pachymeningitis; more prevalent in MPO-ANCA-positive granulomatosis with polyangiitis.

phenotype/spontaneous-abortion.body:
# Spontaneous abortion / pregnancy loss

Loss of pregnancy including resorption of conceptuses and abortion; observed (up to ~58% abortion, plus resorption) in pregnant Wistar rats exposed to calabash chalk.

phenotype/sticky-saliva.body:
# Sticky saliva

A patient-reported xerostomia-related symptom of viscous or sticky saliva, assessed via the EORTC QLQ-H&N35 sticky-saliva (HNSS) domain, that aggravates swallowing and speech.

phenotype/stillbirth.body:
# Stillbirth

Delivery of a non-living fetus; observed in ~5% of fetuses in 400 mg/kg calabash chalk treated pregnant rats.

phenotype/suicidal-ideation.body:
# Suicidal ideation and behavior

Thoughts of or attempts at suicide; severe and subthreshold premenstrual dysphoria are associated with increased suicidal ideation and a significantly elevated risk of suicide attempts.

phenotype/surgical-site-infection.body:
# Surgical site infection

Infection at or near the surgical incision following spinal fusion, ranging from superficial to deep, often polymicrobial; pathogens reported include Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae and others.

phenotype/visual-impairment.body:
# Visual impairment

Reduced visual function ranging from poor acuity to perception of light only, frequently due to optic neuropathy and subsequent optic atrophy in hypertrophic pachymeningitis.

phenotype/wound-complication.body:
# Postoperative wound complication

Any wound-related adverse event following spinal surgery, including surgical site infection, wound dehiscence, hematoma, and seroma, typically defined within 90 days to 6 months postoperatively.

phenotype/wound-dehiscence.body:
# Wound dehiscence

Separation or reopening of the surgical wound edges following spinal surgery, classified as superficial or deep.

population/adolescent-girls.body:
# Adolescent girls

Girls who have attained menarche and are in adolescence; PMDD has been documented in this group with prevalence around 5%, indicating early onset of the disorder.

population/adult-working-women.body:
# Adult working women

Adult women in paid employment, considered a high-risk group for PMDD due to occupational stress and anxiety; in a Hangzhou cross-sectional survey of 1710 such women PMDD prevalence was 3.04%.

population/pediatric-patients.body:
# Pediatric patients

Children and adolescents (approximately ages 3-25 years across these studies) who underwent posterior spinal fusion or spinal instrumentation for scoliosis.

population/pregnant-women.body:
# Pregnant women

Women during pregnancy; the population that most commonly consumes calabash chalk as a remedy for morning sickness, exposing themselves and their fetuses to lead and other contaminants. In a Cameroonian cohort, consumption prevalence was 43.33%, highest among primigravidas.

population/women-of-reproductive-age.body:
# Women of reproductive age

Women between menarche and menopause, the population in which PMS and PMDD occur; PMS prevalence is reported as 10-98% (meta-analytic overall 47.8%) while PMDD affects approximately 2-8% of this population.

stats.effect_size: 3-8% meet strict PMDD criteria; 13-18% have clinically relevant dysphoric PMS

publication/pmid-10709556.body:
# Dental print media and their value in forensic odontology

A survey of 177 forensic identification cases published in German dental print media (1975-1995) and 500 dentists found only 3% of cadavers were identified through dental-print-media recognition, while dental/forensic-odontologic procedures were as important as fingerprints in resolving 56% of identified cases, prompting recommendations to improve case presentation.

extra.name: Dental print media and their value in forensic odontology

publication/pmid-12768646.body:
# How does premenstrual dysphoric disorder relate to depression and anxiety disorders?

Theoretical review arguing that PMDD is a distinct diagnostic entity rather than a variant of depression or an anxiety disorder, with irritability and affect lability as its most characteristic symptoms, and that the rapid-onset efficacy of serotonin reuptake inhibitors reflects serotonergic synapses distinct from their antidepressant/anti-anxiety actions.

extra.name: How does premenstrual dysphoric disorder relate to depression and anxiety disorders?

publication/pmid-12892987.body:
# The prevalence, impairment, impact, and burden of premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMS/PMDD)

Review estimating that 3-8% of reproductive-age women meet strict PMDD criteria and 13-18% have clinically relevant dysphoric premenstrual symptoms, and showing that the impairment, lowered quality of life, and DALY burden of PMS/PMDD are comparable to dysthymia and major depressive disorder.

extra.name: The prevalence, impairment, impact, and burden of premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMS/PMDD)

publication/pmid-15985056.body:
# Possible azithromycin-associated hiccups

A 76-year-old man developed persistent hiccups after a 5-day course of azithromycin for pharyngitis (Naranjo score 5, possible); hiccups resolved after azithromycin discontinuation and baclofen therapy, with a hypothesized vagal mechanism.

publication/pmid-18366818.body:
# The prevalence of premenstrual dysphoric disorder in a randomly selected group of urban and rural women

Prospective cross-sectional study of 1246 randomly sampled US women applying all four DSM-IV research criteria, finding a PMDD prevalence of 1.3% (effect size method) and 1.0% (absolute severity method), far lower than DSM-IV estimates and the 54% rate obtained by retrospective self-report.

extra.name: The prevalence of premenstrual dysphoric disorder in a randomly selected group of urban and rural women

publication/pmid-20172536.body:
# Estrogen receptor alpha (ESR-1) associations with psychological traits in women with PMDD and controls

Case-control genetic association study (68 PMDD women, 56 controls) showing 7 of 25 personality traits differed between groups and that 11 of 12 significant trait associations involved intron 4 SNPs of the estrogen receptor alpha (ESR-1) gene previously linked to PMDD.

extra.name: Estrogen receptor alpha (ESR-1) associations with psychological traits in women with PMDD and controls

publication/pmid-21731343.body:
# Experimental studies of forensic odontology to aid in the identification process

A review of experimental forensic-odontology methods for human identification, covering tooth prints (ameloglyphics / enamel rod end patterns), cheiloscopy (lip prints), rugoscopy (palatal rugae), bite marks, radiography, age and sex estimation, and DNA analysis from dental tissues.

extra.name: Experimental studies of forensic odontology to aid in the identification process

publication/pmid-22375213.body:
# Effects of Pilates Training on Lumbo-Pelvic Stability and Flexibility

Single-blinded RCT in 40 healthy adults found 8 weeks of mat Pilates (45 min, 2x/week) significantly improved sit-and-reach flexibility (P<0.001) and lumbo-pelvic stability (85% passing the test at 8 weeks vs 0% in controls, P<0.001).

extra.name: Effects of Pilates Training on Lumbo-Pelvic Stability and Flexibility

publication/pmid-22977372.body:
# Effect of Calabash Chalk on the Histomorphology of the Gastro-Oesophageal Tract of Growing Wistar Rats

Oral calabash chalk suspension (40 mg/mL) given to growing Wistar rats for 14-28 days caused gastric mucosal oedema with haemorrhages and inflammatory infiltrates, and oesophageal acanthosis, hyperkeratosis and koilocytosis, indicating it compromises the gastro-oesophageal tract.

extra.name: Effect of Calabash Chalk on the Histomorphology of the Gastro-Oesophageal Tract of Growing Wistar Rats

publication/pmid-23335219.body:
# Concise Review: Adult Salivary Gland Stem Cells and a Potential Therapy for Xerostomia

Reviews radiation-induced hyposalivation and the characterization of rodent and human salivary gland stem/progenitor cells, arguing that pre-RT isolation and post-RT autologous transplantation of ductal salivary gland stem cells (e.g. c-Kit+) could provide a durable cell-based cure for xerostomia.

extra.name: Concise Review: Adult Salivary Gland Stem Cells and a Potential Therapy for Xerostomia

publication/pmid-24299643.body:
# 'Eiffel-by-Night': A New MR Sign Demonstrating Reactivation in Idiopathic Hypertrophic Pachymeningitis

Case report of a 47-year-old man with idiopathic hypertrophic pachymeningitis (chronic headache and lower cranial nerve palsies) in whom contrast-enhanced MRI showed a thick hypointense dura with peripheral enhancement of the posterior falx and tentorium, described as the new 'Eiffel-by-Night' sign reflecting central fibrosis and peripheral active inflammation.

extra.name: 'Eiffel-by-Night': A New MR Sign Demonstrating Reactivation in Idiopathic Hypertrophic Pachymeningitis

publication/pmid-25036711.body:
# Neurotrophic factor GDNF promotes survival of salivary stem cells

Identifies a highly enriched murine submandibular gland stem cell population (Lin-CD24+c-Kit+Sca1+) that restores saliva secretion after serial transplantation into irradiated glands, and shows that GDNF is highly expressed in these cells, upregulated by radiation, and improves saliva production and stem-cell survival without accelerating head and neck cancer growth.

extra.name: Neurotrophic factor GDNF promotes survival of salivary stem cells

publication/pmid-25703277.body:
# Clinico-radiological spectrum and outcome in idiopathic hypertrophic pachymeningitis

Retrospective cohort of 28 patients with hypertrophic pachymeningitis (20 idiopathic, 8 secondary) characterizing clinical features (headache 80%, visual symptoms 75%), MRI patterns, treatment, and outcome; the peripheral contrast-enhancement pattern and Eiffel-by-night sign were significantly more common in IHP and the mean clinical score improved from 6.55 to 1.80 after treatment.

extra.name: Clinico-radiological spectrum and outcome in idiopathic hypertrophic pachymeningitis

publication/pmid-26214326.body:
# Wound Closure in Nonidiopathic Scoliosis: Does Closure Matter?

Retrospective chart review of 76 pediatric nonidiopathic scoliosis patients undergoing posterior spinal fusion found that plastic multilayered closure had a 0% wound complication rate versus 19% for nonstandardized orthopedic closure (p=0.007, OR 10.2), with a trend toward fewer returns to the operating room.

extra.name: Wound Closure in Nonidiopathic Scoliosis: Does Closure Matter?

publication/pmid-26545650.body:
# The effects of the Pilates method on hamstring extensibility, pelvic tilt and trunk flexion

Systematic review of 21 studies concluding there is moderate evidence that Pilates practice significantly increases hamstring extensibility, pelvic tilt, and trunk flexion in sedentary and recreationally active people, while a detraining period is associated with gradual loss of these gains.

extra.name: The effects of the Pilates method on hamstring extensibility, pelvic tilt and trunk flexion

publication/pmid-26880659.body:
# The role of stem cells in the prevention and treatment of radiation-induced xerostomia in patients with head and neck cancer

Systematic review of salivary gland stem-cell-based strategies for radiation-induced xerostomia, covering stem cell transplantation, bone marrow-derived cell mobilization, Wnt/beta-catenin and GDNF molecular regulation, the bath-and-shower effect, stem-cell-rich region sparing, submandibular/oral cavity sparing, and adaptive radiotherapy.

extra.name: The role of stem cells in the prevention and treatment of radiation-induced xerostomia in patients with head and neck cancer

publication/pmid-27051220.body:
# Ameloglyphics: A possible forensic tool for person identification following high temperature and acid exposure

An in vitro study of 90 tooth prints from 20 extracted maxillary premolars (cellophane tape technique, analyzed with Verifinger software) showed all 20 original tooth prints were inter- and intra-individually distinct, and that tooth prints remained reproducible with high similarity after exposure to hydrochloric acid (up to 20 min) and heat (up to 750 degrees C).

extra.name: Ameloglyphics: A possible forensic tool for person identification following high temperature and acid exposure

publication/pmid-27263602.body:
# The effect of calabash chalk on some hematological parameters in female adult Wistar rats

In adult female Wistar rats, 40 mg/kg non-salted calabash chalk for 14 days significantly lowered haemoglobin and red blood cell count and raised erythrocyte sedimentation rate, while salted chalk produced no significant haematological change.

extra.name: The effect of calabash chalk on some hematological parameters in female adult Wistar rats

publication/pmid-28123281.body:
# The connecting link! Lip prints and fingerprints

A cross-sectional study of 200 North Indian subjects (100 male, 100 female) recording lip prints and right thumb fingerprints found the branched lip-print pattern predominated in males and the vertical pattern in females, the loop fingerprint predominated in both sexes, and no statistically significant correlation between lip prints and fingerprints within either gender.

extra.name: The connecting link! Lip prints and fingerprints

publication/pmid-28453679.body:
# BioPAXViz: a cytoscape application for the visual exploration of metabolic pathway evolution

Introduces BioPAXViz, a Cytoscape 3 app that parses, views and visually compares metabolic pathway topologies across pre-computed pathway phylogenomic profiles given a species phylogeny, to facilitate the study of metabolic pathway evolution and engineering.

extra.name: BioPAXViz: a cytoscape application for the visual exploration of metabolic pathway evolution

publication/pmid-28584483.body:
# Can dead man tooth do tell tales? Tooth prints in forensic identification

An in vivo study of upper first premolar tooth prints from 80 individuals (acetate peel technique, Verifinger SDK 6.5 and AFIS software) found tooth prints from the same tooth recorded 4-5 months apart matched in 42/80 cases and were distinct between individuals; wavy pattern was the predominant tooth print, and whorl fingerprints tended to co-occur with wavy tooth prints.

extra.name: Can dead man tooth do tell tales? Tooth prints in forensic identification

publication/pmid-29284931.body:
# Are Tooth Prints a Hard Tissue Equivalence of Finger Print in Mass Disaster: A Rationalized Review

A review proposing tooth prints (enamel rod end patterns / ameloglyphics) as a hard-tissue analog to fingerprints for personal identification in mass disasters, describing the basis of enamel rod end patterns, their eight subpattern types, and recording methods (acid etching, acetate peel, automated biometrics).

extra.name: Are Tooth Prints a Hard Tissue Equivalence of Finger Print in Mass Disaster: A Rationalized Review

publication/pmid-29678523.body:
# Safety and Efficacy of Mesenchymal Stem Cells for Radiation-Induced Xerostomia: A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Phase 1/2 Trial (MESRIX)

Randomized, placebo-controlled phase 1/2 trial (MESRIX) of 30 patients showing that ultrasound-guided autologous adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell injection into the submandibular glands was safe and significantly increased unstimulated whole salivary flow rate (33% at 1 month, 50% at 4 months) and improved patient-reported xerostomia outcomes and serous gland tissue.

extra.name: Safety and Efficacy of Mesenchymal Stem Cells for Radiation-Induced Xerostomia: A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Phase 1/2 Trial (MESRIX)

publication/pmid-30598913.body:
# Gestational Toxicity of Calabash Chalk (Nzu) in Wistar Rats

Oral calabash chalk (400 or 800 mg/kg) administered to pregnant Wistar rats throughout gestation inhibited maternal weight gain and reduced implantation sites, fetus number and uterine weight, causing resorption, abortion and stillbirth in a dose-dependent manner (LD50 >5000 mg/kg).

extra.name: Gestational Toxicity of Calabash Chalk (Nzu) in Wistar Rats

publication/pmid-31110448.body:
# Analysis of enamel rod end pattern for personal identification

In 100 families (400 individuals), tooth prints recorded by acetate peel technique and analyzed with VeriFinger SDK v6.7 showed eight distinct enamel rod end subpatterns (wavy branched predominant); patterns were unique to each tooth/individual, differed significantly by gender, and showed familial tendency in incisors, canines and premolars (65%, 66%, 52% of families).

extra.name: Analysis of enamel rod end pattern for personal identification

publication/pmid-31489087.body:
# High umbilical cord blood lead levels and “calabar chalk” consumption amongst pregnant women in two hospitals in Cameroon

In a cross-sectional study of 300 pregnant women in Cameroon, calabar chalk consumption prevalence was 43.33% (highest in primigravidas); umbilical cord blood lead was higher in consumers (31.19 ug/dl) than non-consumers (25.33 ug/dl) but not statistically significant, with extremely high lead levels in both groups.

extra.name: High umbilical cord blood lead levels and “calabar chalk” consumption amongst pregnant women in two hospitals in Cameroon

publication/pmid-32337126.body:
# Forensic Odontology, a Boon and a Humanitarian Tool: A Literature Review

Literature review of forensic odontology methods for human identification, including dental DNA analysis, tooth prints, rugoscopy, cheiloscopy, bite mark analysis, and the use of teeth for sex, age, race and blood group determination; teeth resist decomposition and serve as a reliable identification tool in mass disasters and crimes.

extra.name: Forensic Odontology, a Boon and a Humanitarian Tool: A Literature Review

publication/pmid-32566521.body:
# Scanning Electron Microscope Corroboration of Ameloglyphics - A New Tool in Forensic Odontology

In 10 extracted central incisors, enamel (ink) prints corresponded to enamel prism geometry confirmed by SEM and were grouped into long-prism, short-prism and combination patterns; the technique showed high reproducibility (98-100%) and specificity (100%), establishing SEM corroboration of ameloglyphics for personal identification.

extra.name: Scanning Electron Microscope Corroboration of Ameloglyphics - A New Tool in Forensic Odontology

publication/pmid-32723016.body:
# Trends in Salivary Gland Tissue Engineering: From Stem Cells to Secretome and Organoid Bioprinting

Reviews salivary gland tissue engineering for radiotherapy-induced xerostomia, comparing cell-based strategies (salivary gland stem cells, adipose/bone marrow/dental pulp mesenchymal stem cells), cell-free secretome approaches (cell soups, conditioned media, extracellular vesicles/exosomes), and 3D organoid bioprinting, noting that adipose-derived MSC transplantation is the only strategy that reached phase 1/2 human trials.

extra.name: Trends in Salivary Gland Tissue Engineering: From Stem Cells to Secretome and Organoid Bioprinting

publication/pmid-33223711.body:
# Prevalence of premenstrual dysphoric disorder among school-going adolescent girls

Cross-sectional study of 397 school-going adolescent girls in Chandigarh, India, finding a PMDD prevalence of 4.8% and positive correlations between PMDD severity and perceived stress, depression, and anxiety.

extra.name: Prevalence of premenstrual dysphoric disorder among school-going adolescent girls

publication/pmid-33663193.body:
# Premenstrual syndrome, a common but underrated entity: review of the clinical literature

A clinical review of PMS and PMDD covering epidemiology, etiology (gonadal steroids and neurotransmitters such as serotonin and GABA), DSM-5/ACOG/RCOG/ISPMD diagnostic criteria, and treatment, concluding that SSRIs and combined oral contraceptives are first-line pharmacotherapies.

extra.name: Premenstrual syndrome, a common but underrated entity: review of the clinical literature

publication/pmid-34526851.body:
# Dopamine Agonist-Associated Hiccup in Parkinson's Disease: A Case Report

A 45-year-old man with Parkinson's disease developed persistent hiccups with the dopamine agonists pramipexole and ropinirole (dose-dependent) but not with levodopa, rasagiline, or amantadine, implicating dopamine D3 and serotonergic receptor stimulation.

extra.name: Dopamine Agonist-Associated Hiccup in Parkinson's Disease: A Case Report

publication/pmid-34530168.body:
# Copy number variation profile-based genomic typing of premenstrual dysphoric disorder in Chinese

Genome-wide copy number variations from white blood cell DNA of 127 Chinese PMDD patients and 108 controls were clustered by machine learning into depression (D) and invasion (V) clinical types with 89.0% consistency, and diagnostic CNV features classified genomic groups with 83.0% average accuracy, supporting a predominantly genetic nature of PMDD.

extra.name: Copy number variation profile-based genomic typing of premenstrual dysphoric disorder in Chinese

publication/pmid-34720517.body:
# Forensic Odontological Parameters as Biometric Tool: A Review

Review describing dental biometric tools for human identification - tooth prints (ameloglyphics), dental radiographs, smile, palatal rugae patterns (rugoscopy), lip prints (cheiloscopy) and tongue prints - and the characteristics required of a biometric trait; dental structures survive adverse conditions where conventional biometrics fail.

extra.name: Forensic Odontological Parameters as Biometric Tool: A Review

publication/pmid-35052289.body:
# Effect of Home-Based Tele-Pilates Intervention on Pregnant Women: A Pilot Study

Pilot cluster RCT (14 pregnant women) found 8 weeks of home-based tele-Pilates significantly increased hip joint muscle strength and significantly reduced Oswestry Disability Index and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index versus non-Pilates controls, alleviating pregnancy-induced low back pain and insomnia.

extra.name: Effect of Home-Based Tele-Pilates Intervention on Pregnant Women: A Pilot Study

publication/pmid-35183442.body:
# Marrow derived autologous stromal cells for the restoration of salivary hypofunction (MARSH): study protocol for a phase I dose escalation trial of patients with xerostomia after radiation therapy for head and neck cancer

Protocol for MARSH, a first-in-human single-center phase I 3+3 dose-escalation trial of autologous interferon-gamma-stimulated bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cells injected into the submandibular glands to treat radiation-induced xerostomia, with primary endpoint of recommended phase 2 dose based on dose-limiting toxicity.

extra.name: Marrow derived autologous stromal cells for the restoration of salivary hypofunction (MARSH): study protocol for a phase I dose escalation trial of patients with xerostomia after radiation therapy for head and neck cancer

publication/pmid-35486613.body:
# Long-term Safety of Treatment with Autologous Mesenchymal Stem Cells in Patients with Radiation-Induced Xerostomia: Primary Results of the MESRIX Phase I/II Randomized Trial

Long-term (minimum 2 year) follow-up of the MESRIX randomized placebo-controlled trial showing autologous adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell injection into submandibular glands is safe with no treatment-related serious adverse events, significantly reduces xerostomia questionnaire symptoms, and yields a clinically relevant increase in unstimulated whole saliva flow rate (to 0.20 vs 0.16 mL/min placebo).

extra.name: Long-term Safety of Treatment with Autologous Mesenchymal Stem Cells in Patients with Radiation-Induced Xerostomia: Primary Results of the MESRIX Phase I/II Randomized Trial

publication/pmid-36700097.body:
# BIONDA: a free database for a fast information on published biomarkers

Presents BIONDA, a free text-mining-based online database of molecular biomarkers (genes, proteins, miRNAs) for all diseases, automatically extracted from Europe PMC abstracts and curated against UniProt, Disease Ontology and miRBase, with reliability scoring of biomarker-disease pairs.

extra.name: BIONDA: a free database for a fast information on published biomarkers

publication/pmid-36817713.body:
# Plastic multilayered closure versus orthopedic surgeon closure after spinal instrumentation in pediatric neuromuscular scoliosis

Retrospective comparison of 86 pediatric neuromuscular scoliosis patients found no statistically significant difference in wound complication rate (20.8% OC vs 12.5% PMC, p=0.394) or unplanned return to OR between plastic multilayered closure and orthopedic closure, but PMC had significantly longer operative time (p=0.016) and more patients discharged with a drain.

extra.name: Plastic multilayered closure versus orthopedic surgeon closure after spinal instrumentation in pediatric neuromuscular scoliosis

publication/pmid-37046350.body:
# Efficacy of mesenchymal stem cell therapy in rodent models of radiation-induced xerostomia and oral mucositis: a systematic review

Systematic review of 12 rodent studies (659 animals) finding that MSC therapy (bone-marrow- and adipose-derived) ameliorates radiation-induced xerostomia by increasing salivary protein secretion and salivary flow rate, shortening salivary lag time, and reducing apoptosis, with more modest benefit for radiation-induced oral mucositis.

extra.name: Efficacy of mesenchymal stem cell therapy in rodent models of radiation-induced xerostomia and oral mucositis: a systematic review

publication/pmid-37369596.body:
# Rare case report of moxifloxacin-induced persistent hiccups

A man in his 40s with AIDS treated with moxifloxacin for tuberculous pleurisy developed persistent hiccups (Naranjo score 6, probable) that stopped 2 minutes after intramuscular metoclopramide; proposed mechanism is GABA-receptor competition and gastric stimulation.

extra.name: Rare case report of moxifloxacin-induced persistent hiccups

publication/pmid-37620905.body:
# Maintenance of adult stem cells from human minor salivary glands via the Wnt signaling pathway

In vitro study showing human minor salivary gland stem cells (hMSGSCs) cultured in a 3D Matrigel system maintain stemness (increased LGR5) when the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway is activated (Wnt3A, CHIR99021) and the BMP pathway is inhibited (Noggin), while acinar/duct differentiation markers (AMY1B, MUC5B, KRT19) decrease.

extra.name: Maintenance of adult stem cells from human minor salivary glands via the Wnt signaling pathway

publication/pmid-37654278.body:
# Ameloglyphics: A Forensic Tool for Human Identification

Review of ameloglyphics describing enamel structure and enamel rod (prism) patterns, methods to record enamel rod end patterns (acid etching, acetate peel technique, automated biometrics), and the use of unique tooth prints as a low-cost adjunct biometric tool in forensic odontology.

extra.name: Ameloglyphics: A Forensic Tool for Human Identification

publication/pmid-37658468.body:
# Effectiveness and safety of mesenchymal stem/stromal cell for radiation-induced hyposalivation and xerostomia in previous head and neck cancer patients (MESRIX-III): a study protocol for a single-centre, double-blinded, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase II study

Study protocol for the MESRIX-III phase II randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (n=120) evaluating ultrasound-guided intraglandular allogeneic adipose-derived MSC injection (25x10^6 cells/submandibular gland) versus CryoStor10 placebo for radiation-induced hyposalivation, with change in unstimulated whole saliva flow rate as the primary endpoint.

extra.name: Effectiveness and safety of mesenchymal stem/stromal cell for radiation-induced hyposalivation and xerostomia in previous head and neck cancer patients (MESRIX-III): a study protocol for a single-centre, double-blinded, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase II study

publication/pmid-37671372.body:
# Pilates-based therapeutic exercise for pregnancy-related low back and pelvic pain: A prospective, randomized, controlled trial

Single-blinded RCT (34 pregnant women with lumbopelvic pain) found 12 weeks of Pilates added to usual prenatal care significantly improved disability (RMDQ), pain (VAS), and mood (HADS-A, HADS-D) versus controls, with no significant change in sleep quality (PSQI).

extra.name: Pilates-based therapeutic exercise for pregnancy-related low back and pelvic pain: A prospective, randomized, controlled trial

publication/pmid-37979696.body:
# Plastic surgeon closure is comparable to orthopedic closure when a perioperative optimization protocol is instituted for pediatric patients with neuromuscular scoliosis

Retrospective cohort of 81 pediatric neuromuscular scoliosis patients undergoing spinal fixation under a perioperative optimization protocol found that plastic multilayered closure did not reduce wound complications or surgical site infections compared with standard orthopedic closure, but resulted in longer surgery, longer drain duration, and more postoperative transfusions.

extra.name: Plastic surgeon closure is comparable to orthopedic closure when a perioperative optimization protocol is instituted for pediatric patients with neuromuscular scoliosis

publication/pmid-38038413.body:
# Post-radiation xerostomia therapy with allogeneic mesenchymal stromal stem cells in patients with head and neck cancer: study protocol for phase I clinical trial

Phase I non-randomized open-label study protocol enrolling 10 oropharyngeal cancer patients with post-radiation xerostomia and 10 healthy controls to evaluate the safety and preliminary efficacy of allogeneic umbilical-cord-derived MSCs injected into both parotid (50x10^6 cells) and submandibular (25x10^6 cells) glands, with salivary flow, scintigraphy, MRI, and biopsy assessments.

extra.name: Post-radiation xerostomia therapy with allogeneic mesenchymal stromal stem cells in patients with head and neck cancer: study protocol for phase I clinical trial

publication/pmid-38091917.body:
# GABAergic Neuroactive Steroid Response to Sertraline in Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder

In an open-label study of 35 controls and 27 women with PMDD, luteal-phase sertraline (50 mg) significantly increased serum pregnanolone and the pregnanolone:progesterone ratio and decreased 3a,5a-androsterone, but did not change allopregnanolone; no luteal-phase neuroactive steroid differences were found between PMDD and controls.

extra.name: GABAergic Neuroactive Steroid Response to Sertraline in Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder

publication/pmid-38365799.body:
# Gingival-derived mesenchymal stem cell therapy regenerated the radiated salivary glands: functional and histological evidence in murine model

Controlled guinea pig study in which intravenous allogeneic gingival mesenchymal stem cells (GMSCs) homed to 15 Gy-irradiated parotid glands and restored salivary flow rate, body weight, gland weight, and normal acinar/ductal histology, with increased PCNA proliferation and decreased apoptosis.

extra.name: Gingival-derived mesenchymal stem cell therapy regenerated the radiated salivary glands: functional and histological evidence in murine model

publication/pmid-38430363.body:
# Mesenchymal Stromal/Stem Cell Therapy Improves Salivary Flow Rate in Radiation-Induced Salivary Gland Hypofunction in Preclinical in vivo Models: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

Systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 preclinical in vivo studies (858 animals; 13 in meta-analysis) finding MSC therapy significantly increases salivary flow rate after radiation (SMD 6.99, 95% CI 2.55-11.42) with no serious adverse events, with intraglandular delivery outperforming systemic, and improvements in acinar tissue, vascular areas, and paracrine factors.

extra.name: Mesenchymal Stromal/Stem Cell Therapy Improves Salivary Flow Rate in Radiation-Induced Salivary Gland Hypofunction in Preclinical in vivo Models: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

publication/pmid-38441659.body:
# Mesenchymal Stem/Stromal Cell Therapy for Radiation-Induced Xerostomia in Previous Head and Neck Cancer Patients: A Phase II Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Trial

Phase II randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial (MESRIX-III, n=120) of intraglandular allogeneic adipose-derived MSCs versus placebo for radiation-induced xerostomia; ASC therapy significantly increased unstimulated whole saliva flow rate by 38% from baseline (placebo non-significant 21%), but no statistically significant superiority over placebo was demonstrated; treatment was safe with 32% developing de novo HLA class I donor-specific antibodies.

extra.name: Mesenchymal Stem/Stromal Cell Therapy for Radiation-Induced Xerostomia in Previous Head and Neck Cancer Patients: A Phase II Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Trial

publication/pmid-38450348.body:
# Antibiotic-Induced Hiccups: A Case Report and Brief Literature Review

First reported case of cefotaxime-induced hiccups in a 38-year-old man after appendectomy, with hiccups recurring after each cefotaxime injection and resolving on withdrawal; includes a brief literature review of antibiotic-induced hiccups attributing a likely GABA-antagonism mechanism.

extra.name: Antibiotic-Induced Hiccups: A Case Report and Brief Literature Review

publication/pmid-38544793.body:
# Evaluation of prenatal calabash chalk geophagy on the developing brain of Wistar rats

Prenatal calabash chalk (200 or 800 mg/kg, GD7-20) in Wistar rats lowered pup birth weight and transiently delayed surface righting reflex at 800 mg/kg but produced no lasting hippocampal/cortical cytoarchitectural, myelin or glial alterations; concluded prenatal exposure at these doses may not be deleterious to the developing brain after exposure ceases. ICP-MS confirmed aluminium, lead, vanadium, arsenic and other metals in the chalk.

extra.name: Evaluation of prenatal calabash chalk geophagy on the developing brain of Wistar rats

publication/pmid-38578768.body:
# Long-Term Outcome Following Treatment With Allogeneic Mesenchymal Stem/Stromal Cells for Radiation-Induced Hyposalivation and Xerostomia

Three-year follow-up of the open-label phase I MESRIX-II trial in 10 oropharyngeal-cancer survivors showed that allogeneic adipose-derived MSC injections into the parotid and submandibular glands were safe (no treatment-related SAEs, no donor-specific antibodies at 3 years) and produced a sustained ~28% increase in stimulated salivary flow rate and reduced xerostomia symptoms.

extra.name: Long-Term Outcome Following Treatment With Allogeneic Mesenchymal Stem/Stromal Cells for Radiation-Induced Hyposalivation and Xerostomia

publication/pmid-38759113.body:
# Distinct features of ANCA-associated hypertrophic pachymeningitis compared with other etiologies: findings from a study of 74 patients

Retrospective single-centre cohort of 74 hypertrophic pachymeningitis patients showing ANCA-associated vasculitis (all GPA) and Mycobacterium tuberculosis as the predominant etiologies; GPA-HP was associated with headache, cranial neuropathy, peripheral enhancement and the Eiffel-by-night sign, while infectious HP showed hypoglycorrhachia, brain parenchymal lesions and stroke.

extra.name: Distinct features of ANCA-associated hypertrophic pachymeningitis compared with other etiologies: findings from a study of 74 patients

publication/pmid-39060406.body:
# The use of stem cells in treating xerostomia: a systematic review

PRISMA systematic review of 19 in vitro, in vivo, and clinical studies on stem-cell therapy for xerostomia, concluding that diverse stem-cell sources (bone marrow, adipose, salivary-gland, dental-pulp) and organoids can reverse hyposalivation from radiotherapy and Sjogren-like causes.

extra.name: The use of stem cells in treating xerostomia: a systematic review

publication/pmid-39180335.body:
# BioASQ Synergy: a dialogue between question-answering systems and biomedical experts for promoting COVID-19 research

Describes BioASQ Synergy, an iterative dialogue framework between biomedical experts and automated question-answering systems for answering open COVID-19 research questions, and reports a proof-of-concept across three task versions using the CORD-19 dataset.

extra.name: BioASQ Synergy: a dialogue between question-answering systems and biomedical experts for promoting COVID-19 research

publication/pmid-39183328.body:
# Salivary gland organoid transplantation as a therapeutic option for radiation-induced xerostomia

Developed clinically suitable collagen-based human salivary gland organoids that self-renew and differentiate into acinar/ductal cells; xenotransplanted hSGOs engrafted and expressed MUC5B in a mouse xerostomia model, and allogeneic mSGO transplantation regenerated damaged acini and increased salivation.

extra.name: Salivary gland organoid transplantation as a therapeutic option for radiation-induced xerostomia

publication/pmid-39396054.body:
# Adipose derived or bone-marrow derived mesenchymal stem cell treatment for hyposalivation: protocol for a systematic review and network meta-analysis

Protocol (PROSPERO CRD42024527183) for a systematic review and network meta-analysis to indirectly compare change in unstimulated salivary flow rate between adipose-derived and bone-marrow-derived MSC treatment in patients with hyposalivation from radiotherapy or Sjogren's syndrome.

extra.name: Adipose derived or bone-marrow derived mesenchymal stem cell treatment for hyposalivation: protocol for a systematic review and network meta-analysis

publication/pmid-39403910.body:
# Prevalence and Correlations of Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder: A Sample of Adult Working Women

A cross-sectional survey of 1710 adult working women in Hangzhou, China found a PMDD prevalence of 3.04% and identified age, age at menarche, income, menstrual cycle regularity, menstrual symptoms, physical activity, and caffeine intake as independent influencing factors by logistic regression.

extra.name: Prevalence and Correlations of Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder: A Sample of Adult Working Women

publication/pmid-39477435.body:
# Salivary Gland Volume Predicts Malnutrition in Irradiated Head and Neck Cancer Patients: A Prospective Analysis

Prospective analysis of 61 head-and-neck cancer patients undergoing (chemo-)radiotherapy found that baseline parotid gland volume (threshold 55.3 cm3), rather than radiation dosimetric parameters, was an independent predictor of malnutrition; submandibular gland volume showed no such association.

extra.name: Salivary Gland Volume Predicts Malnutrition in Irradiated Head and Neck Cancer Patients: A Prospective Analysis

publication/pmid-39555889.body:
# RankMHC: Learning to Rank Class-I Peptide-MHC Structural Models

Presents RankMHC, a Learning-to-Rank (LambdaMART/XGBoost) predictor that ranks ensembles of class-I peptide-MHC structural conformations by closeness to the native structure, outperforming classical protein-ligand and prior ML-based pMHC scoring functions across multiple alleles and peptide lengths.

extra.name: RankMHC: Learning to Rank Class-I Peptide-MHC Structural Models

publication/pmid-39724130.body:
# Reliability of ameloglyphics in forensic identification: a systematic review

PRISMA systematic review of 18 studies (1189 teeth) on ameloglyphics; all studies reported inter- and intra-individual variation confirming tooth print uniqueness, but 3 studies found no sex-specific pattern and methodological/classification heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis, concluding ameloglyphics is a reliable adjunct (not standalone) tool for forensic identification.

extra.name: Reliability of ameloglyphics in forensic identification: a systematic review

publication/pmid-39766181.body:
# Clinical Introduction of Stem Cell Sparing Radiotherapy to Reduce the Risk of Xerostomia in Patients with Head and Neck Cancer

Multicenter planning study showing that stem-cell-sparing radiotherapy can be implemented in routine practice with small adjustments, reducing mean dose to parotid stem-cell-rich regions and lowering predicted xerostomia complication probabilities with photon therapy without compromising target coverage.

extra.name: Clinical Introduction of Stem Cell Sparing Radiotherapy to Reduce the Risk of Xerostomia in Patients with Head and Neck Cancer

publication/pmid-8619448.body:
# Severe hiccups secondary to doxycycline-induced esophagitis during treatment of malaria

A 51-year-old man treated with quinine and doxycycline for Plasmodium falciparum malaria developed intractable hiccups caused by a doxycycline-induced esophageal erosion and ulcer; symptoms resolved with omeprazole and sucralfate after drug discontinuation.

extra.name: Severe hiccups secondary to doxycycline-induced esophagitis during treatment of malaria

social-factor/low-income.body:
# Low income

Low personal or household income/socioeconomic status; in adult working women, lower income showed a significant negative correlation with PMDD prevalence (i.e. higher income was protective), attributed to reduced life-quality, limited healthcare access, and elevated work-related stress.

social-factor/sex.body:
# Sex

The male/female categorization of an individual, a target of forensic identification; lip print and fingerprint pattern distributions differ by sex (e.g., branched lip prints in males, vertical in females).

structure/enamel-rod.body:
# Enamel rod

The fundamental microscopic building block of enamel (approximately 4-5 micrometres in diameter) laid down by ameloblasts in an undulating, intertwining path; groups of rods running in different directions create distinct patterns of rod endings on the tooth surface.

structure/hiccup-reflex-arc.body:
# Hiccup reflex arc

The neural circuit generating hiccups, composed of an afferent limb (phrenic, vagal and sympathetic T6-T12 fibers), a poorly defined central mediator (brainstem/midbrain, between cervical C3-C5 and the brainstem), and an efferent limb (primarily the phrenic nerve with accessory nerves to the diaphragm and intercostal muscles).

structure/peptide-mhc-complex.body:
# Peptide-MHC complex

The structural complex formed by a peptide bound in the class-I MHC binding cleft; pMHC structural models are ensembles of candidate peptide poses whose binding mode (pose closest to the native structure, measured by full-atom LRMSD) RankMHC identifies.

study/marsh-trial.body:
# MARSH trial

A first-in-human single-center phase I 3+3 dose-escalation trial with expansion cohort (NCT04489732, University of Wisconsin) of autologous interferon-gamma-stimulated bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cells injected into the submandibular glands of head and neck cancer patients with radiation-induced xerostomia; primary endpoint is the recommended phase 2 dose determined by dose-limiting toxicity.
synonyms: Marrow derived Autologous stromal cells for the Restoration of Salivary Hypofunction

study/mesrix.body:
# MESRIX trial

An investigator-initiated, single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 1/2 trial (NCT02513238, Copenhagen) of autologous adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell (2.8 million ASCs/cm3) injection versus placebo into the submandibular glands of 30 HPV+ oropharyngeal carcinoma patients with radiation-induced xerostomia, with short-term (4-month) and long-term (>=2-year) endpoints.
synonyms: Mesenchymal Stem cells for Radiation-Induced Xerostomia

study/mesrix-ii.body:
# MESRIX-II

A clinical safety study (n=10) by Lynggaard et al. of intraglandular off-the-shelf allogeneic adipose-derived MSCs for radiation-induced xerostomia, reporting no serious adverse reactions and an increase in saliva production of about 46% at 4 months.

study/mesrix-iii.body:
# MESRIX-III

A single-centre, double-blinded, randomised, placebo-controlled phase II clinical trial (NCT04776538, n=120) in Denmark evaluating ultrasound-guided intraglandular allogeneic adipose-derived MSCs versus CryoStor10 placebo in the submandibular glands for radiation-induced hyposalivation and xerostomia in previous head and neck cancer patients.

study/post-radiation-xerostomia-umbilica.body:
# Allogeneic umbilical cord MSC post-radiation xerostomia phase I study

A non-randomized, single-centre, open-label phase I exploratory clinical trial (NCT06012604) at the Institute of Oncology Ljubljana evaluating the safety and preliminary efficacy of allogeneic umbilical-cord-derived MSCs injected into parotid and submandibular glands in 10 oropharyngeal cancer patients with post-radiation xerostomia.

extra.name: Allogeneic umbilical cord MSC post-radiation xerostomia phase I study

synonyms: Treatment of Post-radiation Xerostomia with Allogeneic Mesenchymal Stromal Stem Cells pilot study

variant/esr1-intron-4-snps.body:
# ESR1 intron 4 SNPs

A cluster of single nucleotide polymorphisms located in intron 4 of the ESR1 (estrogen receptor alpha) gene, in tight linkage disequilibrium, previously associated with PMDD and associated with personality traits (harm avoidance, neuroticism, emotional stability, abstractedness) distinguishing PMDD patients from controls.
synonyms: estrogen receptor alpha intron 4 single nucleotide polymorphisms

variant/gabrb2-copy-number-variation.body:
# GABRB2 copy number variations

Copy number variations located at the esv2730987 and nsv1177513 sites of the GABRB2 gene that were found to be significantly associated with PMDD and schizophrenia in Chinese and with schizophrenia in Germans, linking GABA-A receptor genetics to PMDD susceptibility.

variant/pmdd-diagnostic-cnv-features.body:
# PMDD diagnostic copy number variation features

Germline copy number gain (CNVG) and loss (CNVL) features called from 100 kb white blood cell DNA sequence windows that segregate PMDD patient genomes into the D (depression-type) and V (invasion-type) clinical groups; hundreds of such diagnostic features overlap with susceptibility genes/pathways and serve as molecular markers for clinical typing of PMDD.

extra.name: PMDD diagnostic copy number variation features
